# Local systems with restricted variation on the formal punctured disc via factorization

**Authors:** Ekaterina Bogdanova Address: Harvard University, USA Email address: ebogdanova@math.harvard.edu

## Abstract

We define the stack of $G$ -local systems with restricted variation on the formal puntured disc and study its properties. We embed sheaves of categories over this stack into the category of factorization module categories over $\Rep(G)$ . Along the way we develop a theory of factorization structures in families and study functorialities of such under changes of the base curve.

## 1. Introduction

Let $k$ be a ground field of characteristic zero, $G$ be a split connected reductive group over $k$ , $\check{G}$ be the Langlands dual group to $G$ .

#### 1.0.1. Local geometric Langlands

The local geometric Langlands program from [FG06] suggests that, roughly speaking, DG categories strongly acted on by the loop group $LG$ are equivalent to categories over the moduli space of $\check{G}$ -local systems on the formal punctured disc, i.e. $\check{G}$ -bundles on the formal punctured disc with connection. The equivalence reads as

$$ {\mathbb{L}}:\D(LG)\mathbf{-ModCat}\xrightarrow{\sim}\QCoh(\LocSys_{\check{G}}(D^{\circ}))\mathbf{-ModCat}. $$

The first orienting remark is that ${\mathbb{L}}$ does not preserve the functor of forgetting the module structures. Rather ${\mathbb{L}}$ should be thought of as a categorical Morita equivalence.

Local geometric Langlands is supposed to satisfy various compatibilities as in the arithmetic theory, e.g. there should be a compatibilities with parabolic induction and with Whittaker models.

There are a number of examples providing the evidence for the existence of such an equivalence. Among them are derived Satake equivalence ([BF08]), Bezrukavnikov’s theory ([Bez16]), works of Frenkel-Gaitsgory ([FG04], [FG06], [FG09a], [FG09b], [FG09c]) and Raskin ([Rasb], [Ras21b]). One expects that these works combined with the compatibilities are supposed to pin down the equivalence ${\mathbb{L}}$ .

One distinguishing feature of this setup is the geometry on the set of spectral parameters, which has led to the suggestion (c.f. [BD04]) that pointwise spectral descriptions should extend in families over these moduli spaces. More precisely, there should be a natural functor (different from ${\mathbb{L}}$ )

$$ \D(LG)\mathbf{-ModCat}\rightarrow\QCoh(\LocSys_{\check{G}}(D^{\circ}))\mathbf{-ModCat} $$

preserving the functor forgetting the module structures.

#### 1.0.2. A sibling: restricted local geometric Langlands.

A recent progress in local arithmetic Langlands has been the formulation of the conjecture using families of Galois representations ([Zhu21]). Roughly speaking, it says that there exists a fully faithful functor from representations of $G({\mathbb{F}}_{q}((t)))$ to (appropriately understood) coherent sheaves on a certain stack parametrizing Galois representations.

In an unpublished work, Gaitsgory came up with a categorical incarnation of this conjecture, which provides a link (via methods of [AGK+22]) between geometric and arithmetic worlds. Moreover, Gaitsgory‘s conjecture is suited to any ground field and any sheaf theory. It roughly states that there exists a natural equivalence

$$ {\mathbb{L}}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}:LG\mathbf{-ModCat}_{{\operatorname{restr}}}\xrightarrow{\sim}\QCoh(\LocSys_{\check{G}}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))\mathbf{-ModCat}, $$

where on the left-hand side we have to work with a subtler notion of categorical representation (in order to fix an issue with the failure of Kunneth formula in the constructible setting), and on the right-hand side we need accordingly to replace $\LocSys_{\check{G}}(D^{\circ})$ by the moduli of local systems with restricted variation.

### 1.1. Statement of the result

Let $X$ be a smooth affine curve, $x\in X$ be a closed point. Let $U=X\setminus x_{0}$ .

One of the difficulties in local geometric Langlands is the fact that $\LocSys_{\check{G}}(D^{\circ})$ is complicated as an algebro-geometric object. For instance, this is not an Artin stack, and it is not even locally of finite type. One way to avoid dealing with this problem is to introduce an additional structure on the objects with rather simple geometry. Namely, factorization structure. The general heuristic is that factorization structures tend to ”decrease the complexity” in the following sense. A factorization algebra whose fibers involve only the formal disc will have invariants encoding the information about the whole formal punctured disc. For instance, factorization geometry of Beilinson-Drinfeld grassmannian encodes usual geometry of the loop group, and factorization geometry of classifying space of $\check{G}$ encodes geometry of $\check{G}$ -local systems on the formal punctured disc. We refer to [Rasa] for a more detailed introduction to the factorizable geometry.

#### 1.1.1. From local systems on the punctured disc to factorization modules over $\Rep(\check{G})$ .

#### Conjecture 1.

There exists a fully faithful functor

$$ \mathbf{Fact}:\QCoh(\LocSys_{\check{G}}(D^{\circ}))\mathbf{-ModCat}\rightarrow\Rep({\check{G}})\mathbf{-FactModCat} $$

that preserves the forgetful functors from both sides to $\mathbf{DGCat}$ . Here

- - On the left-hand side $\QCoh(\LocSys_{\check{G}}(D^{\circ}))$ is viewed as a monoidal category with usual tensor product.

- - On the right-hand side $\Rep({\check{G}})$ is the DG category of representation of ${\check{G}}$ equipped with factorization algebra category structure coming from symmetric monoidal structure on $\Rep({\check{G}})$ .

#### 1.1.2.

As in [CFGY24, 1.1.1], the functor will be given as tensor product with a certain factorization $\Rep({\check{G}})$ -module category, $\mathbf{Fact}(\QCoh(\LocSys_{\check{G}}(D^{\circ})))$ , equipped with a commuting action of $\QCoh(\LocSys_{\check{G}}(D^{\circ})$ . The fiber at $x$ of this category will identify with $\QCoh(\LocSys_{\check{G}}(D^{\circ}))$ , and the action will be given by tensor product of quasi-coherent sheaves. In more detail, $\mathbf{Fact}(\QCoh(\LocSys_{\check{G}}(D^{\circ})))$ is defined as the category of quasi-coherent sheaves on a certain factorization prestack $\LocSys_{\check{G}}(D^{\circ}_{{\operatorname{Ran}}})$ degenerating $\LocSys_{\check{G}}(D)$ to $\LocSys_{\check{G}}(D^{\circ})$ .

In this paper we prove an analogue of Conjecture 1 in the context of restricted local geometric Langlands. Before we formulate the statement, we need to introduce the replacement for the left-hand side of the Conjecture 1.

#### 1.1.3. The stack of local systems with restricted variation on the puntured disc.

Although our main theorem is in the de Rham setting, we define and study the stack of local systems with restricted variation on the puntured disc in all three frameworks: Betti, de Rham, and etale. We refer to the introduction of [AGK+22] for the overview of the idea of local systems with restricted variation. Here we highlight the features of the local context.

- • In the Betti situation $\QLisse(D^{\circ})$ is equivalent to $\QLisse({\mathbb{G}}_{m})$ , so we can directly use results from [AGK+22].

- • Let us turn to the de Rham context. Although it is complicated to define the category of all $D$ -modules on the formal punctured disc, distinguishing the subcategory of lisse ones is rather straightforward. We set $\Lisse(D^{\circ})$ to be the category of free $k((t))$ -modules of finite rank equipped with a connection. We also define

$$ \QLisse(D^{\circ})=\IndLisse(D^{\circ}). $$

Note that this category is already left complete, which is not always the case in the global setting.

- • In the etale context we define $\Lisse(D^{\circ})$ to be the category of lisse $\ell$ -adic sheaves on $\Spec(k((t)))$ , and $\QLisse(D^{\circ}):=\IndLisse(D^{\circ}).$ Here characteristic of $k$ could be greater than zero.

Results of Katz ([Kat87], [Kat86]) provide a connection between $\QLisse(D^{\circ})$ and $\QLisse({\mathbb{G}}_{m})$ in de Rham and etale situations. Namely, we have a section of a natural restriction map

$$ \QLisse({\mathbb{G}}_{m})\rightarrow\QLisse(D^{\circ}). $$

For an affine test scheme $S=\Spec(A)$ , an $S$ -point of $\LocSys_{\check{G}}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})$ is symmetric monoidal functor

$$ \Rep({\check{G}})\rightarrow\QLisse(D^{\circ})\otimes(A\Mmod). $$

Note that (1.3) implies that there is a section of a natural map

$$ \LocSys_{\check{G}}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}({\mathbb{G}}_{m})\rightarrow\LocSys_{\check{G}}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}). $$

We remark that unlike the global case, the stack $\LocSys_{\check{G}}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})$ is classical. Nevertheless, we still must work in the context of derived algebraic geometry.

As in the global case, the stack $\LocSys_{\check{G}}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})$ splits into a disjoint union of prestacks ${\mathcal{Z}}_{\sigma}$ parameterized by isomorphism classes of semi-simple ${\check{G}}$ -local systems $\sigma$ on $D^{\circ}$ , and each ${\mathcal{Z}}_{\sigma}$ can be written as a quotient of a formal affine scheme by ${\check{G}}$ .

#### 1.1.4. Main result.

#### Theorem 1.2.

There exists a fully faithful functor

$$ \mathbf{Fact}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}:\QCoh(\LocSys_{\check{G}}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))\mathbf{-ModCat}\rightarrow\Rep({\check{G}})\mathbf{-FactModCat} $$

that preserves the forgetful functors from both sides to $\mathbf{DGCat}$ . Here

- - On the left-hand side $\QCoh(\LocSys_{\check{G}}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))$ is viewed as a monoidal category with usual tensor product.

- - On the right-hand side $\Rep({\check{G}})$ is the DG category of representation of ${\check{G}}$ equipped with factorization algebra category structure coming from symmetric monoidal structure on $\Rep({\check{G}})$ .

#### 1.2.1.

As in Conjecture 1, the functor $\mathbf{Fact}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}$ is given by a certain factorization $\Rep({\check{G}})$ -module category, $\mathbf{Fact}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(\QCoh(\LocSys_{\check{G}}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})))$ , equipped with a commuting action of $\QCoh(\LocSys_{\check{G}}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))$ . We deinfe $\mathbf{Fact}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(\QCoh(\LocSys_{\check{G}}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})))$ as the category of quasi-coherent sheaves on the prestack

$$ \LocSys_{\check{G}}(D^{\circ}_{{\operatorname{Ran}}})\times_{\LocSys_{\check{G}}(D^{\circ})}\LocSys_{\check{G}}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}). $$

### 1.3. Motivation

#### 1.3.1.

First, we provide pieces of motivation of why one might expect such a statement to be true. In topology, the analogue of Conjecture 1 and Theorem 1.2 are transparent. Namely, the parallel to factorization structure in algebraic geometry is ${\mathbb{E}}_{2}$ -structure in topology, so we are interested in the category of ${\mathbb{E}}_{2}$ -modules over $\Rep(\check{G})$ (this is a symmetric monoidal category, so, in particular, an ${\mathbb{E}}_{2}$ -category). But recall that for any ${\mathbb{E}}_{2}$ -category $\mathbf{A}$ one has

$$ \mathbf{A}\Mmod^{{\mathbb{E}}_{2}}\cong(\int_{S^{1}}\mathbf{A})\Mmod, $$

where on the right-hand side we consider left modules over chiral homology of $\mathbf{A}$ . We can also rewrite

$$ (\int_{S^{1}}\mathbf{A})\Mmod\cong\HH(\mathbf{A})\Mmod. $$

So for $\mathbf{A}=\Rep(\check{G})$ we get

$$ \Rep(\check{G})\Mmod^{{\mathbb{E}}_{2}}\cong\QCoh(\Loc_{\check{G}}(S^{1}))\Mmod. $$

#### 1.3.2.

Next we discuss how Theorem 1.2 fits in the context of restricted local Langlands conjecture 1.2. One prediction of the local restricted Langlands correspondence is that any $\mathbf{C}\in LG\mathbf{-ModCat}_{{\operatorname{restr}}}$ is fibered over $\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})$ , i.e. one expects there to be a natural functor (parallel to (1.1))

$$ \D(LG)\mathbf{-ModCat}_{{\operatorname{restr}}}\dashrightarrow\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))\mathbf{-ModCat} $$

that preserves the forgetful functors from both sides to $\mathbf{DGCat}$ . This functor would serve as the spectral decomposition in local restricted geometric Langlands program. Let us outline the construction of this functor.

#### 1.3.3.

There is a dual statement to Conjecture 1 which is the main theorem of [CFGY24]:

#### Theorem 1.4.

If $G$ is connected and reductive, then there is a fully faithful functor:

$$ \mathbf{Fact}:\D(LG)\mathbf{-ModCat}\to\D(\operatorname{Gr}_{G})\mathbf{-FactModCat} $$

that preserves the forgetful functors from both sides to $\mathbf{DGCat}$ .

Above:

- • In the left-hand side, $\D(LG)$ is the DG category of D-modules on the loop group $LG$ , equipped with the convolution monoidal structure.

- • On the right-hand side, $\D(\operatorname{Gr}_{G})$ is the DG category of D-modules on the affine Grassmannian $\operatorname{Gr}_{G}$ , equipped with the factorization algebra category structure inherited from the factorization structure of the Beilinson–Drinfeld affine Grassmannians .

The fully faithful functor $\mathbf{Fact}$ is also given by a “bimodule” object equipped with commuting actions of $\D(LG)$ (in the usual sense) and $\D(\operatorname{Gr}_{G})$ (in the factorization sense). The underlying DG category of this bimodule is just $\D(LG)$ .

#### Corollary 1.4.1.

If $G$ is connected and reductive, then there is a fully faithful functor:

$$ \mathbf{Fact}:\D(LG)\mathbf{-ModCat}_{{\operatorname{restr}}}\to\D(\operatorname{Gr}_{G})\mathbf{-FactModCat} $$

that preserves the forgetful functors from both sides to $\mathbf{DGCat}$ .

The desired functor (1.4) would make the following diagram commute: This follows by definition from the fact that for $f:\Spec(A)\rightarrow\operatorname{Ran}_{X_{\mathrm{dR}},x}$ the diagram

$$ {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\D(LG)\mathbf{-ModCat}_{{\operatorname{restr}}}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\QCoh(\LocSys_{\check{G}}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))\mathbf{-ModCat}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\D(\operatorname{Gr}_{G})\mathbf{-FactModCat}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Rep({\check{G}})\mathbf{-FactModCat},} $$

where the bottom functor is given by restriction along the (factorization) Satake functor

$$ \operatorname{Sat}:\Rep({\check{G}})\to\D(\operatorname{Gr}_{G}). $$

#### 1.4.2.

It will follow from this construction that for any ${\check{G}}$ -local system $\sigma$ on the punctured disk and ${\mathbf{M}}\in\mathbf{ShvCat}(\operatorname{LocSys}_{{\check{G}}}(D^{\circ}))$ , the fiber DG category ${\mathbf{M}}_{\sigma}$ can be described as

$$ {\mathbf{M}}_{\sigma}\simeq R_{{\check{G}},\sigma}\operatorname{-FactMod}(\check{\mathbf{Fact}}({\mathbf{M}})), $$

where $R_{{\check{G}},\sigma}$ is a factorization algebra object in $\operatorname{Rep}({\check{G}})$ obtained by twisting the regular representation $R_{\check{G}}$ by $\sigma$ . As an application, for any categorical representations $\mathbf{C}$ of $LG$ and a ${\check{G}}$ -local system $\sigma$ on the punctured disk, we obtain a conjectural description of the fiber of the spectral decomposition of $\mathbf{C}$ at $\sigma$ . Namely, we conjecture it to be

$$ \operatorname{Sat}(R_{{\check{G}},\sigma})\operatorname{-FactMod}(\mathbf{Fact}(\mathbf{C})). $$

### 1.5. Outline of the argument

Below we highlight the main ideas that go into the proof of Theorem 1.2.

We first notice that the question is of purely local nature, so should be independent of what curve we are using. To that end, for a map of curves $f:X\rightarrow Y$ we develop a notion of pullback of factorization structures and prove that for a fixed $\mathbf{A}\in\mathbf{FactAlg}({\operatorname{Ran}}_{Y})$ we have

$$ f^{!}:\mathbf{A}-\mathbf{FactMod}({\operatorname{Ran}}_{Y,y})\xrightarrow{\sim}f^{!}(\mathbf{A})-\mathbf{FactMod}({\operatorname{Ran}}_{X,x}). $$

We also prove that (1.5) is compatible with the functor $\mathbf{Fact}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}$ in the sense that the following diagram commutes

$$ {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Rep({\check{G}})-\mathbf{FactMod}({\operatorname{Ran}}_{Y,y})} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\QCoh(\LocSys_{\check{G}}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))\mathbf{-ModCat}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Rep({\check{G}})-\mathbf{FactMod}({\operatorname{Ran}}_{X,x}).} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{Fact}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}_{Y}} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{Fact}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}_{X}} $$

Taking $f$ to be a smooth function on $X$ we reduce to the case $X={\mathbb{A}}^{1}$ , $x=0$ .

Let ${\mathbf{C}}_{1}$ and ${\mathbf{C}}_{2}$ be DG categories acted on by $\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})$ . Theorem 3.8 asserts that the functor

$$ \operatorname{Fun}_{\QCoh(\LocSys_{\check{G}}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))}({\mathbf{C}}^{1},{\mathbf{C}}^{2})\rightarrow\operatorname{FactFun}_{\Rep({\check{G}})}(\mathbf{Fact}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}({\mathbf{C}}^{1}),\mathbf{Fact}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}({\mathbf{C}}^{2})) $$

is an equivalence. Let us illustrate the plan of the proof in the simplest case: when ${\mathbf{C}}_{i}$ for $i=1,2$ are $\Vect$ as plain categories, but the action of $\QCoh(\LocSys_{\check{G}}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))$ is via pullback to a point $\pt_{\sigma_{i}}$ corresponding to a local system on the punctured disc. Denote these ${\mathbf{C}}_{i}$ by $\Vect_{\sigma_{i}}$ .

Then left-hand side of (1.7) has a clear geometric meaning:

$$ \operatorname{Fun}_{\QCoh(\LocSys_{\check{G}}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))}({\mathbf{C}}^{1},{\mathbf{C}}^{2})\cong\QCoh(\pt_{\sigma_{1}}\times_{\LocSys_{\check{G}}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})}\pt_{\sigma_{2}}). $$

In order to give a geometric description of the category on the right-hand side of (1.7), we use tools introduced in [CFGY24] for working with factorization modules. Also, to avoid complicated geometry of the formal punctured disc we use [Kat87, Theorem 2.4.10], which allows us to extend $\sigma_{i}$ to local systems $\widetilde{\sigma}_{1}$ on ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ . Combining these methods, we get

$$ \operatorname{FactFun}_{\Rep({\check{G}})}(\mathbf{Fact}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}({\mathbf{C}}^{1}),\mathbf{Fact}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}({\mathbf{C}}^{2}))\cong{\prescript{}{\widetilde{\sigma}_{1}}{R_{{\check{G}}}}}_{\widetilde{\sigma}_{2}}\operatorname{-FactMod}. $$

Here ${\prescript{}{\widetilde{\sigma}_{1}}{R_{\check{G}}}}_{\widetilde{\sigma}_{2}}$ is a factorization algebra obtained by twisting the regular representation $R_{\check{G}}$ by $\widetilde{\sigma}_{1}$ and $\widetilde{\sigma}_{2}$ . Note that

$$ {\prescript{}{\widetilde{\sigma}_{1}}{R_{\check{G}}}}_{\widetilde{\sigma}_{2}} $$

is a commutative factorization algebra corresponding to the D-scheme $\Isom(\widetilde{\sigma}_{1},\widetilde{\sigma}_{2})$ . But Beilinson-Drinfeld theory of chiral algebras gives a concise geometric description of the category of modules over such factorization algebras: the answer is the category of quasi-coherent sheaves of the space of horizontal sections of the corresponding D-scheme on the punctured disc. It is left to notice that in the case of the D-scheme $\Isom(\widetilde{\sigma}_{1},\widetilde{\sigma}_{2})$ it is precisely

$$ \QCoh(\pt_{\sigma_{1}}\times_{\LocSys_{\check{G}}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})}\pt_{\sigma_{2}}). $$

### 1.6. Notation and conventions

Denote by $X$ a fixed smooth and connected (but not necessarily proper) curve over $k$ .

#### 1.6.1. Lie theory.

Let $G$ be a connected reductive group with a fixed standard Borel $B$ and a maximal torus $T$ . Let $(\check{\Lambda},\check{\Delta},\Lambda,\Delta)$ denote the root datum corresponding to $(G,T)$ . Langlands duality attaches to every $(G,T)$ a dual group $(\check{G},\check{T})$ with root datum $(\Lambda,\Delta,\check{\Lambda},\check{\Delta})$ .

We define the loop group ind-scheme $LG$ (resp. the arc group scheme $L^{+}G$ ) as

$$ LG(\Spec A):=G(\Spec A((t))), $$

$$ L^{+}G(\Spec A):=G(\Spec A[[t]]). $$

We define the affine Grassmannian as the fppf quotient

$$ \Gra_{G}:=LG/L^{+}G. $$

#### 1.6.2. Higher categories.

We will substantially use the language of $\infty$ -categories as developed in [Lur09]. We write category for an $(\infty,1)$ -category unless specified otherwise. Our main result is a statement about $(\infty,2)$ -categories. We refer to [GR17a], [Che24], [CF24] and [CFGY24] for the overview of relevant foundations of $(\infty,2)$ -categories. We write ${\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}$ for an $(\infty,1)$ -category of $(\infty,1)$ -categories and $\mathbf{Cat}_{\infty}$ for its enhancement to an $(\infty,2)$ -category. We write $\BiCat$ for an $(\infty,1)$ -category of $(\infty,2)$ -categories and $\mathbf{BiCat}_{\infty}$ for its enhancement to an $(\infty,2)$ -category.

#### 1.6.3. Higher algebra.

We will also use higher algebra as in [Lur17]. We will denote by $\Vect$ the stable category of chain complexes of vector spaces over $k$ . This category is equipped with a natural symmetric monoidal structure (in ther sense of $\infty$ -categories).

#### 1.6.4. DG categories.

By a DG category we mean a category equipped with a module structure over $\Vect$ with respect to the symmetric monoidal structure on the category of presentable stable categories given by the Lurie tensor product. DG categories form an $(\infty,1)$ -category (where 1-morphisms are colimit-preserving functors) denoted by $\DGCat$ , which carries a symmetric monoidal structure via Luire tensor product. Denote by $\mathbf{DGCat}$ its enhancement to an $(\infty,2)$ -category. In particular, we can talk about algebras in $\mathbf{DGCat}$ and modules over them. For an algebra ${\mathbf{A}}$ in $\mathbf{DGCat}$ denote the $(\infty,2)$ -category of modules over it by ${\mathbf{A}}-\mathbf{ModCat}$ . Unless specified otherwise, all monoidal DG categories will be assumed unital. We also utilize the formalism of categorical invariant/coinvatiants developed in [Ber17].

Given a DG category $\mathbf{C}$ we can talk about t-structures on it. Given a t-structure we denote by

$$ \mathbf{C}^{\leq 0},\text{ }\mathbf{C}^{\geq 0},\mathbf{C}^{\heartsuit} $$

the corresponding subcategories according to the cohomological conventions.

#### 1.6.5. Derived algebraic geometry.

Most of the geometry in the present paper is taking place at the spectral side of local geometric Langlands, where we must work in the context derived algebraic geometry as in [GR17a]. We begin with the category $\AffSch$ of derived affine schemes over $k$ . All of our geometric objects can be viewed as either a prestack, i.e. a functor

$$ \AffSch^{\op}\rightarrow{\operatorname{Grpd}}_{\infty}, $$

or an lax prestack, i.e. a functor

$$ \AffSch^{\op}\rightarrow{\operatorname{Cat}}_{\infty}. $$

By a stack we will mean a prestack satisfying etale descent. We denote by $\laxPreSt_{\Corr}$ the category of lax prestacks with morphisms given by correspondences.

### 1.7. Organization of the paper

In Section 2 we recall the notions and statements regarding factorization structures relevant to the present paper. In Section 3 we define our main geometric object: the stack of local systems with restricted variation on the formal punctured disc, and study its relationship to the existing moduli stack in the de Rham setting. We define the functor in Theorem 1.2 and formulate our main result. In Section 4 we perform a series of reductions of the statement of Theorem 1.2. Namely, we first reduce to the case when $X={\mathbb{A}}^{1}$ . Next, recall that Theorem 1.2 asserts that the functor

$$ \operatorname{Fun}_{\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))}({\mathbf{C}}^{1},{\mathbf{C}}^{2})\rightarrow\operatorname{FactFun}_{\Rep(G)}(\mathbf{Fact}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}({\mathbf{C}}^{1}),\mathbf{Fact}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}({\mathbf{C}}^{2})) $$

is an equivalence. We reduce to the case when ${\mathbf{C}}^{1}\cong\QCoh(R_{1})$ and ${\mathbf{C}}^{2}\cong\QCoh(R_{2})$ , where the action of $\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})$ on $\QCoh(R_{i})$ comes from a pullback along a map $R_{i}\rightarrow\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})$ . We then describe both sides of (1.8) explicitly. In Section 5 we conclude the proof of Theorem 1.2 using this description. In Appendix A we recall the notion of multidiscs and describe the correct may to descend multidiscs to the de Rham prestack. We define the factorization prestack degenerating horizontal jets into a fixed prestack ${\mathcal{Y}}$ to meromorphic horizontal jets into ${\mathcal{Y}}$ and its parameterized analogue. In Appendix B we study functoriality of factorization patterns under etale pullbacks of the base curve. In Appendix C we establish foundations of parameterized crystals of categories and parameterized factorization patterns. Finally, in Appendix D we describe in geometric terms the category of (parameterized) factorization modules over a commutative (parameterized) factorization algebra.

## 2. Preliminaries on factorization structures

In this section we give a somewhat informal introduction to the formalism of factorization geometry. Everything apart from subsections 2.5 and 2.7 has appeared in either [BD04], [Rasa], [CF24] or [CFGY24].

### 2.1. Factorization algebras

#### 2.1.1. Ran space and crystals of categories.

#### Definition 2.1.2.

The unital Ran space of $X$ , denoted by ${\operatorname{Ran}}$ , is a lax prestack that assigns to $S\in\AffSch$ the category ${\operatorname{Ran}}(S)$ of finite subsets of $X(S)$ , where morphisms are given by inclusions of subsets.

#### Remark 2.1.3.

Definition 2.1.2 makes sense for any prestack $Y$ in place of $X$ . We will use the notation ${\operatorname{Ran}}_{Y}$ in such cases.

#### Definition 2.1.4 ([CF24]).

Let $Y$ be a laft11 1 I.e. as a functor $\operatorname{AffSch}^{\operatorname{op}}\to\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty}$ it is obtained by left Kan extension along its restriction on the category of affine schemes of finite type $\operatorname{AffSch}_{\operatorname{ft}}\subset\operatorname{AffSch}$ . lax prestack. A crystal of categories ${\mathbf{A}}$ on $Y$ consists of the following data:

- • For any $s:S\to Y$ with $S$ a finite type affine scheme, there is a $\D(S)$ -module DG category:

### 2.2. Factorization modules

#### Definition 2.2.1.

Let $Y$ be a lax prestack. Define $\operatorname{Arr}(Y)$ to be the lax prestack such that

$$ \operatorname{Arr}(Y)(S):=\operatorname{Arr}(Y(S)), $$

i.e. the category of arrows in $Y(S)$ .

Let $p_{s},p_{t}:\operatorname{Arr}(Y)\to Y$ be the morphisms remembering respectively the sources and the targets of the arrows.

#### Definition 2.2.2.

Let $x$ be a closed point of $X$ and $\underline{x}:\operatorname{pt}\to{\operatorname{Ran}}$ be the corresponding morphism. The Ran space with a marked point $x$ is the lax prestack ${\operatorname{Ran}}$ defined as the following fiber product:

$$ \textstyle{{\operatorname{Ran}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \textstyle{\operatorname{Arrow}({\operatorname{Ran}})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \scriptstyle{p_{s}} \textstyle{\operatorname{pt}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \scriptstyle{\underline{x}} \textstyle{{\operatorname{Ran}}.} $$

Unless otherwise stated, we always view ${\operatorname{Ran}}$ as a lax prestack over ${\operatorname{Ran}}$ by the composition

$$ {\operatorname{Ran}}\to\operatorname{Arrow}({\operatorname{Ran}})\xrightarrow{p_{t}}{\operatorname{Ran}}. $$

#### Remark 2.2.3.

By definition, knowing a $k$ -valued point of ${\operatorname{Ran}}$ is equivalent to knowing a finite subset $\underline{y}$ of closed points of $X$ such that $\underline{x}\subset\underline{y}$ .

#### Construction 2.2.4.

For ${\operatorname{Ran}}$ as above, let $({\operatorname{Ran}}\times{\operatorname{Ran}})_{\operatorname{disj}}$ be the following fiber product:

$$ \textstyle{({\operatorname{Ran}}\times{\operatorname{Ran}})_{\operatorname{disj}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \scriptstyle{j} \textstyle{{\operatorname{Ran}}\times{\operatorname{Ran}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \textstyle{({\operatorname{Ran}}\times{\operatorname{Ran}})_{\operatorname{disj}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \scriptstyle{j} \textstyle{{\operatorname{Ran}}\times{\operatorname{Ran}},} $$

where we abuse notation by denoting the top horizontal morphism, which is an schematic open embedding, by the same letter $j$ .

We have an obvious schematic étale morphism $\operatorname{add}:({\operatorname{Ran}}\times{\operatorname{Ran}})_{\operatorname{disj}}\to{\operatorname{Ran}}$ .

The correspondence

$$ \textstyle{({\operatorname{Ran}}\times{\operatorname{Ran}})_{\operatorname{disj}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \scriptstyle{j} \scriptstyle{\operatorname{add}} \textstyle{{\operatorname{Ran}}\times{\operatorname{Ran}}} \textstyle{\operatorname{Ran}} $$

makes ${\operatorname{Ran}}$ a ${\operatorname{Ran}}$ -module object in the category of lax prestacks with morphisms given by correspondences.

#### 2.2.5. Factorization module categories

#### Definition 2.2.6.

Let ${\mathbf{A}}$ be a factorization algebra category. A factorization ${\mathbf{A}}$ -module category supported on ${\operatorname{Ran}}$ consists of the following data:

- • An object

$$ {\mathbf{C}}\in\mathbf{CrysCat}({\operatorname{Ran}}); $$

- • An equivalence

$$ \operatorname{act}:j^{\bullet}({\mathbf{C}}\boxtimes{\mathbf{A}})\to\operatorname{add}^{\bullet}({\mathbf{C}}) $$

in $\mathbf{CrysCat}(({\operatorname{Ran}}\times{\operatorname{Ran}})_{\operatorname{disj}})$ ;

- • Higher compatibilities between the above morphism and the ${\operatorname{Ran}}$ -module structure on ${\operatorname{Ran}}$ defined in Construction 2.2.4.

#### Definition 2.2.7 ([CF24]).

Let ${\mathbf{A}}$ be a factorization algebra category and ${\mathbf{C}}$ be a factorization ${\mathbf{A}}$ -module category supported on ${\operatorname{Ran}}$ . We define the core of ${\mathbf{C}}$ to be ${\mathbf{C}}_{x}:=i^{\bullet}{\mathbf{C}}$ , where $i:\operatorname{pt}\to{\operatorname{Ran}}$ is the morphism corresponding to $\underline{x}\subset\underline{x}$ .

We also say ${\mathbf{C}}_{x}$ is a factorization ${\mathbf{A}}$ -module category concentrated at $x$ .

#### Definition 2.2.8.

Similar to Definition 2.1.13, given a morphism $\Phi:{\mathbf{A}}_{1}\to{\mathbf{A}}_{2}$ in $\mathbf{FactAlgCat}$ , and factorization ${\mathbf{A}}_{i}$ -module categories ${\mathbf{C}}_{i}$ , we can define the notion of factorization functors $\Xi:{\mathbf{C}}_{1}\to{\mathbf{C}}_{2}$ that intertwine the action of $\Phi$ . Let

$$ \operatorname{FactFun}_{\Phi}({\mathbf{C}}_{1},{\mathbf{C}}_{2}) $$

be the $\infty$ -category of such functors.

When $\Phi$ is strictly unital, we say $\Xi$ is strictly unital if its underlying morphism in $\mathbf{CrysCat}({\operatorname{Ran}})$ is strict. Let

$$ \operatorname{FactFun}_{{\operatorname{str}},\Phi}({\mathbf{C}}_{1},{\mathbf{C}}_{2})\subset\operatorname{FactFun}_{\Phi}({\mathbf{C}}_{1},{\mathbf{C}}_{2}) $$

be the full subcategory of strictly unital factorization functors.

When $\Phi=\Id_{\mathbf{A}}$ is the identity functor, we also write

$$ \operatorname{FactFun}_{{\operatorname{str}},{\mathbf{A}}}({\mathbf{C}}_{1},{\mathbf{C}}_{2})\subset\operatorname{FactFun}_{{\mathbf{A}}}({\mathbf{C}}_{1},{\mathbf{C}}_{2}) $$

for the above inclusion, call their objects strictly unital factorization ${\mathbf{A}}$ -linear functors.

#### Notation 2.2.9.

Similar to Notation 2.1.15, let

$$ \mathbf{FactModCat} $$

be the $(\infty,2)$ -category such that:

- • An object is a pair $({\mathbf{A}},{\mathbf{C}})$ such that ${\mathbf{A}}$ is a factorization algebra category and ${\mathbf{C}}$ is a factorization ${\mathbf{A}}$ -module category;

- • A morphism is a pair $(\Phi,\Xi):({\mathbf{A}}_{1},{\mathbf{C}}_{1})\to({\mathbf{A}}_{2},{\mathbf{C}}_{2})$ of factorization functors such that $\Xi$ intertwines the action of $\Phi$ .

Let

$$ \mathbf{FactModCat}^{\operatorname{str}}\subset\mathbf{FactModCat} $$

be the 1-full subcategory containing strictly unital factorization functors as morphisms.

Consider the obvious forgetful functor

$$ \mathbf{FactModCat}\to\mathbf{FactAlgCat} $$

For an object ${\mathbf{A}}$ in the target, we denote the fiber at it to be

$$ {\mathbf{A}}\mathbf{-FactModCat}. $$

#### Remark 2.2.10.

By [CF24, Lemma B.5.11] the similarly defined category

$$ {\mathbf{A}}\mathbf{-FactModCat}^{{\operatorname{str}}} $$

coincides with ${\mathbf{A}}\mathbf{-FactModCat}.$

#### 2.2.11. Factorization modules.

#### Definition 2.2.12.

Let ${\mathbf{A}}$ be a factorization algebra category and ${\mathbf{C}}$ be a factorization ${\mathbf{A}}$ -module category. Similar to Definition 2.1.17, we define

$$ \operatorname{FactMod}({\mathbf{A}},{\mathbf{C}}):=\operatorname{FactFun}((\Vect,\Vect),({\mathbf{A}},{\mathbf{C}})). $$

For a factorization algebra ${\mathcal{A}}\in\operatorname{FactAlg}({\mathbf{A}})$ , define

$$ {\mathcal{A}}\operatorname{-FactMod}({\mathbf{C}}):=\operatorname{FactMod}({\mathbf{A}},{\mathbf{C}})\times_{\operatorname{FactAlg}({\mathbf{A}})}\{{\mathcal{A}}\}, $$

and call its objects factorization ${\mathcal{A}}$ -modules in ${\mathbf{C}}$ .

#### Definition 2.2.13.

For

$$ ({\mathcal{A}},{\mathcal{C}})\in\operatorname{FactMod}({\mathbf{A}},{\mathbf{C}}), $$

the core of ${\mathcal{C}}$ is defined to be the restriction of the corresponding global section along $i:\operatorname{pt}\to{\operatorname{Ran}}$ , i.e., the object

$$ {\mathcal{C}}_{x}\in{\mathbf{C}}_{x}. $$

We also say ${\mathcal{C}}_{x}$ is a factorization ${\mathcal{A}}$ -module concentrated at ${\mathbf{C}}_{x}$ .

#### Lemma 2.2.14 ([CF24]).

Let ${\mathbf{A}}$ be a factorization algebra category and ${\mathbf{C}}$ be a factorization ${\mathbf{A}}$ -module category. Then the functor

$$ \operatorname{unit}_{\mathbf{A}}\operatorname{-FactMod}({\mathbf{C}})\to{\mathbf{C}}_{x},\;{\mathcal{C}}\mapsto{\mathcal{C}}_{x} $$

is an equivalence.

#### 2.2.15. Factorization restriction of modules.

One of the important ingredients in the proof of Theorem 1.2 is the following general result established in [CF24].

#### Theorem 2.3 ([CF24]).

Given a morphism $\Phi:{\mathbf{A}}_{1}\to{\mathbf{A}}_{2}$ in the target, there exists a natural contravariant functor

$$ \mathbf{Res}_{\Phi}:{\mathbf{A}}_{2}\mathbf{-FactMod}\to{\mathbf{A}}_{1}\mathbf{-FactMod}, $$

we call it the factorization restriction functor along $\Phi$ . Moreover, for ${\mathbf{C}}_{2}\in{\mathbf{A}}_{2}\mathbf{-FactMod}$ , there is a canonical equivalence

$$ \mathbf{Res}_{\Phi}({\mathbf{C}}_{2})_{x}\simeq\Phi(\operatorname{unit}_{{\mathbf{A}}_{1}})\operatorname{-FactMod}({\mathbf{C}}_{2}). $$

In particular, if $\Phi$ is strictly unital, then $\mathbf{Res}_{\Phi}({\mathbf{C}}_{2})$ and ${\mathbf{C}}_{2}$ have equivalent cores.

#### Proposition 2.3.1 ([CF24]).

Let $\Phi:{\mathbf{A}}\to{\mathbf{A}}^{\prime}$ be a morphism in $\mathbf{FactAlgCat}$ and ${\mathbf{C}}^{\prime}\in{\mathbf{A}}^{\prime}\mathbf{-FactMod}$ . Let ${\mathcal{A}}\in\operatorname{FactAlg}({\mathbf{A}})$ . Then there is a canonical equivalence

$$ {\mathcal{A}}\operatorname{-FactMod}(\mathbf{Res}_{\Phi}({\mathbf{C}}^{\prime}))\simeq\Phi({\mathcal{A}})\operatorname{-FactMod}({\mathbf{C}}^{\prime}). $$

#### Definition 2.3.2 ([CF24]).

Let ${\mathbf{A}}$ be a factorization algebra category and ${\mathbf{C}}$ be a factorization ${\mathbf{A}}$ -module category. Let $\phi:{\mathcal{A}}_{1}\to{\mathcal{A}}_{2}$ be a morphism in $\operatorname{FactAlg}({\mathbf{A}})$ , viewed as a 2-morphism in $\mathbf{FactAlgCat}$ . Then we have a factorization $\Vect_{\operatorname{Ran}}$ -linear functor

$$ \mathbf{Res}_{{\mathcal{A}}_{2}}(\Vect_{{\operatorname{Ran}}})\to\mathbf{Res}_{{\mathcal{A}}_{1}}(\Vect_{{\operatorname{Ran}}}). $$

The core of it is a functor

$$ {\mathcal{A}}_{2}\operatorname{-FactMod}({\mathbf{C}})\to{\mathcal{A}}_{1}\operatorname{-FactMod}({\mathbf{C}}), $$

which we denote by $\operatorname{Res}_{\phi}$ and call it the factorization restriction functor along $\phi$ .

#### 2.3.3. The basic adjunction

Recall that for any $(\infty,2)$ -category ${\mathbf{E}}$ , we have the notion of adjunctions in ${\mathbf{E}}$ . Namely, it consists of a diagram

$$ F:U\rightleftarrows V:G $$

and 2-morphisms $F\circ G\to\Id_{V}$ , $\Id_{U}\to G\circ F$ satisfying the usual axioms.

#### Lemma 2.3.4 ([CF24]).

Let

$$ \Phi:{\mathbf{A}}\rightleftarrows{\mathbf{A}}^{\prime}:\Psi $$

be an adjunction in the 2-category $\mathbf{FactAlgCat}$ . Then $\Phi$ is strictly unital.

The following result follows from Theorem 2.3.

#### Theorem 2.4 ([CF24]).

Let $\Phi:{\mathbf{A}}\rightleftarrows{\mathbf{A}}^{\prime}:\Psi$ be an adjunction in the 2-category $\mathbf{FactAlgCat}$ . Then there is a canonical adjunction in $\mathbf{BiCat}_{\infty}$ :

$$ \mathbf{Res}_{\Phi}:{\mathbf{A}}^{\prime}\mathbf{-FactMod}\rightleftarrows{\mathbf{A}}\mathbf{-FactMod}:\mathbf{Res}_{\Psi}. $$

#### Remark 2.4.1.

Let $\Phi:{\mathbf{A}}\rightleftarrows{\mathbf{A}}^{\prime}:\Psi$ be an adjunction in the 2-category $\mathbf{FactAlgCat}$ . Note that

- (1) For ${\mathbf{C}}^{\prime}\in{\mathbf{A}}^{\prime}\mathbf{-FactModCat}$ , the core of $\mathbf{Res}_{\Phi}({\mathbf{C}}^{\prime})$ is equivalent to that of ${\mathbf{C}}^{\prime}$ because $\Phi$ is strictly unital.

- (2) For ${\mathbf{C}}\in{\mathbf{A}}\mathbf{-FactModCat}$ , the core of $\mathbf{Res}_{\Psi}({\mathbf{C}})$ is equivalent to $\Psi(\operatorname{unit}_{{\mathbb{A}}})\operatorname{-FactMod}({\mathbf{C}})$ .

Hence we can formulate the basic adjunction as the following equivalence:

$$ \operatorname{FactFun}_{{\mathbf{A}}}({\mathbf{C}}^{\prime}_{x},{\mathbf{C}}_{x})\simeq\operatorname{FactFun}_{{\mathbf{A}}^{\prime}}({\mathbf{C}}^{\prime}_{x},\Psi(\operatorname{unit}_{{\mathbf{A}}})\operatorname{-FactMod}_{{\mathbf{C}}_{x}}), $$

where we use the point of view of factorization module categories concentrated at $x$ (rather than supported on ${\operatorname{Ran}}$ ).

### 2.5. Factorization patterns in families

In the present paper we will need to use a slight generalization of the above formalism. Namely, we need factorization patterns in families parameterized by a fixed prestack $S$ with some condition that make technical work easier: we require $S$ to be 1-affine and the category $\QCoh(S)$ to be semi-rigid (see [AGK+22, Appendix C] for what this means).

First, we informally formulate a $S$ -linear version of the notion of crystal of categories on a lax prestack.

#### Definition 2.5.1.

Let $Y$ be a laft lax prestack. A $S$ -linear crystal of categories ${\mathbf{A}}$ on $Y$ consists of the following data:

- • For any $s:R\to Y$ with $R$ being a finite type affine scheme, there is a $\D(R)\otimes\QCoh(S)$ -module DG category:

$$ {\mathbf{A}}_{s}\in\D(R)\otimes\QCoh(S)-\mathbf{ModCat}. $$

- • For any 2-cell $\textstyle{R\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$ $\scriptstyle{s}$ $\scriptstyle{\theta}$ $\textstyle{T\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$ $\scriptstyle{v}$ $\scriptstyle{t}$ $\textstyle{Y,}$ there is a functor

$$ \theta_{\dagger}:{\mathbf{A}}_{s}\to{\mathbf{A}}_{t} $$

intertwining the symmetric monoidal functor

$$ u^{!}\otimes\Id:\D(S)\otimes\QCoh(S)\to\D(T)\otimes\QCoh(S), $$

such that if $\theta$ is invertible, then the induced functor

$$ \D(T)\otimes_{\D(S)}{\mathbf{A}}_{s}\to{\mathbf{A}}_{t} $$

is an equivalence.

- • Certain higher compatibilities.

#### Notation 2.5.2.

Let

$$ \mathbf{CrysCat}^{S}(Y),\;\mathbf{CrysCat}^{S}(Y)^{\operatorname{str}} $$

be the $(\infty,2)$ -category of crystals of categories on $Y$ , with 1-morphisms given by morphisms (resp. strict morphisms) between crystals of categories, and 2-morphisms given by natural transformations.

#### Remark 2.5.3.

Replacing

$$ \mathbf{CrysCat}\text{ }(\text{resp. }\mathbf{CrysCat}(Y)^{\operatorname{str}}) $$

by

$$ \mathbf{CrysCat}^{S}\text{ }(\text{resp. }\mathbf{CrysCat}^{S}(Y)^{\operatorname{str}}) $$

everywhere we obtain the analogues of the definitions and statements presented in this section. We discuss the proofs and definitions in more detail in Appendix C.

#### Example 2.5.4.

Given ${\mathbf{A}}\in\mathbf{FactAlgCat}$ we can construct

$$ {\mathbf{A}}^{S}:={\mathbf{A}}\otimes\QCoh(S)\in\mathbf{FactAlgCat}^{S}. $$

### 2.6. Commutative factorization algebra objects

The identity morphism of ${\operatorname{Ran}}$ upgrades to a map of commutative algebras given by the correspondence (2.1) and the map $\widetilde{\add}$ .

#### Definition 2.6.1.

A multiplicative $S$ -linear crystal of categories ${\mathbf{A}}$ on ${\operatorname{Ran}}$ consists of the following data:

- • An object

$$ {\mathbf{A}}\in\mathbf{CrysCat}^{S}({\operatorname{Ran}}), $$

- • An isomorphism

$$ \operatorname{unit}:\Vect^{S}_{\operatorname{pt}}\to\emptyset_{\operatorname{pt}}^{\bullet}({\mathbf{A}}) $$

in $\mathbf{CrysCat}^{S}(\operatorname{pt})$ ;

- • An isomorphism

$$ \operatorname{mult}:{\mathbf{A}}\boxtimes{\mathbf{A}}\to{\widetilde{\add}}^{\bullet}({\mathbf{A}}) $$

in $\mathbf{CrysCat}^{S}(({\operatorname{Ran}}\times{\operatorname{Ran}}))$ ;

- • Higher compatibilities.

#### Remark 2.6.2.

Note that the data in Definition 2.6.1 has underlying data of lax $S$ -linear factorization algebra category.

#### Definition 2.6.3.

A commutative $S$ -linear factorization algebra category is a multiplicative $S$ -linear crystal of categories, whose underlying data of lax $S$ -linear factorization algebra category is strict. Denote this category by $\mathbf{CFactAlgCat}^{S}$ .

#### Definition 2.6.4.

Similarly, for ${\mathbf{A}}\in\mathbf{CFactAlgCat}^{S}$ we can define commutative $S$ -linear factorization algebras in ${\mathbf{A}}$ . Denote this category by ${\operatorname{CFactAlg}}^{S}({\mathbf{A}}).$

#### Example 2.6.5.

An element ${\mathbf{C}}\in\CommAlg(\mathbf{DGCat})$ can be upgraded to an element in $\mathbf{CFactAlgCat}^{S}$ , denoted by ${\mathbf{C}}^{S}$ .

#### Lemma 2.6.6 ([Ras18, Lemma 8.10.1]).

For ${\mathbf{C}}$ as in Example 2.6.5, the restriction functor to $X$ induces an equivalence

where ${\mathbf{C}}^{S}_{X}$ is the pullback of ${\mathbf{C}}^{S}$ along $X\rightarrow{\operatorname{Ran}}$ .
