## 3. Statement of the result

Since we are going to work only on the spectral side of the equivalence ${\mathbb{L}}$ , we will change the notation and replace $\check{G}$ by $G$ . Let $X$ be a smooth affine curve, $x\in X$ be a closed point. Let $U=X\setminus x$ .

Recall the statement of Conjecture 1:

#### Conjecture.

There exists a fully faithful functor

$$ \mathbf{Fact}:\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}(D^{\circ}))\mathbf{-ModCat}\rightarrow\Rep(G)\mathbf{-FactModCat} $$

that is compatible with the forgetful functors from both sides to $\mathbf{DGCat}$ . Here

- - On the left-hand side $\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}(D^{\circ}))$ is viewed as a monoidal category with usual tensor product. The left-hand side is the $(\infty,2)$ -category of modules for this monoidal category.

- - On the right-hand side $\Rep(G)$ is the DG category of representations of $G$ equipped with factorization algebra category structure coming from the symmetric monoidal structure on $\Rep(G)$ .

### 3.1. Construction of the functor

In this subsection we present a construction of the functor $\mathbf{Fact}$ from Conjecture 1.

#### 3.1.1.

Recall from [Ras18, 9.4] the definition of the factorization lax prestack $\LocSys_{G}(D)_{\operatorname{Ran}_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}}$ :

#### Definition 3.1.2.

For any test affine scheme $S$ the category $\Omega^{1}_{X}(D)_{\operatorname{Ran}_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}}(S)$ is defined as follows:

- • An object is a pair $(s,\omega)$ consisting of an object $s\in\operatorname{Ran}_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}(S)$ and $\omega\in\Gamma(D_{s},\Omega^{1}_{X}\boxtimes{\mathcal{O}}_{S})$ ;

- • A morphism from $(s,\omega)$ to $(s^{\prime},\omega^{\prime})$ consists of a morphism $s\rightarrow s^{\prime}$ in $\operatorname{Ran}_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}(S)$ and an isomorphism between $\omega$ and $\omega^{\prime}|_{D_{s}}$ .

#### Definition 3.1.3.

For any test affine scheme $S$ the category $G(D)_{\operatorname{Ran}_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}}(S)$ is defined as follows:

- • An object is a pair $(s,g)$ consisting of an object $s\in\operatorname{Ran}_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}(S)$ and $g\in\Maps(D_{s},G)$ ;

- • A morphism from $(s,g)$ to $(s^{\prime},g^{\prime})$ consists of a morphism $s\rightarrow s^{\prime}$ in $\operatorname{Ran}_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}(S)$ and an isomorphism between $\omega$ and $g^{\prime}|_{D_{s}}$ .

#### Definition 3.1.4.

We set

$$ \LocSys_{G}(D)_{\operatorname{Ran}_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}}:=(\Lie(G)\otimes\Omega^{1}_{X}(D)_{\operatorname{Ran}_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}})/G(D)_{\operatorname{Ran}_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}}. $$

By [Ras18, Lemma 9.8.1] we have an equivalence of factorization algebra categories:

$$ \QCoh(\LocSys_{G}(D)_{\operatorname{Ran}_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}})\cong\Rep(G). $$

#### 3.1.5.

We will define $\mathbf{Fact}(\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}(D^{\circ})))$ as the category of quasi-coherent sheaves on the $\LocSys_{G}(D)_{\operatorname{Ran}_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}}$ -module lax prestack to be denoted $\LocSys_{G}(D^{\circ}_{{\operatorname{Ran}}})$ .

#### Definition 3.1.6.

Define the prestack $\Omega^{1}(D^{\circ}_{{\operatorname{Ran}}})$ degenerating $\Omega^{1}(D)$ to $\Omega^{1}(D^{\circ})$ as follows. For any test affine scheme $S$ the category $\Omega^{1}(D^{\circ}_{{\operatorname{Ran}}})(S)$ is defined as follows:

- • An object is a pair $(s,\omega)$ consisting of an object $s\in\operatorname{Ran}_{X_{\mathrm{dR}},x}(S)$ and $\omega\in\Gamma(D_{s}\times_{X}U,\Omega^{1}_{U}\boxtimes{\mathcal{O}}_{S})$ ;

- • A morphism from $(s,\omega)$ to $(s^{\prime},\omega^{\prime})$ consists of a morphism $s\rightarrow s^{\prime}$ in $\operatorname{Ran}_{X_{\mathrm{dR}},x}(S)$ and an isomorphism between $\omega$ and $\omega^{\prime}|_{(D_{s}\times_{X}U)}$ .

#### Definition 3.1.7.

Define the prestack $G(D^{\circ}_{{\operatorname{Ran}}})$ degenerating $G(D)$ to $G(D^{\circ})$ as follows. For any test affine scheme $S$ the category $G(D^{\circ}_{{\operatorname{Ran}}})(S)$ is defined as follows:

- • An object is a pair $(s,g)$ consisting of an object $s\in\operatorname{Ran}_{X_{\mathrm{dR}},x}(S)$ and $g\in\Maps(D_{s}\times_{X}U,G)$ ;

- • A morphism from $(s,g)$ to $(s^{\prime},g^{\prime})$ consists of a morphism $s\rightarrow s^{\prime}$ in $\operatorname{Ran}_{X_{\mathrm{dR}},x}(S)$ and an isomorphism between $g$ and $g^{\prime}|_{D_{s}\times_{X}U}$ .

#### Definition 3.1.8.

Set

$$ \LocSys_{G}(D^{\circ}_{{\operatorname{Ran}}}):=(\Lie(G)\otimes\Omega^{1}(D^{\circ}_{{\operatorname{Ran}}}))/G(D^{\circ}_{{\operatorname{Ran}}}). $$

It is clear that $\LocSys_{G}(D^{\circ}_{{\operatorname{Ran}}})$ has a factorization $\LocSys_{G}(D)_{\operatorname{Ran}_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}}$ -module structure.

#### Remark 3.1.9.

Note that

$$ \begin{split}\LocSys_{G}(D^{\circ}_{{\operatorname{Ran}}})_{x}(S)=\Lie(G)\otimes\Gamma(S\times(X^{\wedge}_{x})^{\aff}\times_{X}U,\Omega_{U}^{1}\boxtimes{\mathcal{O}}_{S})/\Hom(S\times(X^{\wedge}_{x})^{\aff}\times_{X}U,G)\cong\\
\cong\LocSys_{G}(D^{\circ})(S).\end{split} $$

#### Remark 3.1.10.

Consider any $s\in\operatorname{Ran}_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}(\Spec(A))$ and $x_{A}:\Spec(A)\rightarrow x\rightarrow\operatorname{Ran}_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}$ . Note that the map $D_{x_{A}}\rightarrow D_{s}$ induces a map

$$ \LocSys_{G}(D^{\circ}_{{\operatorname{Ran}}})\rightarrow\LocSys_{G}(D^{\circ}), $$

and therefore endow $\mathbf{Fact}(\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}(D^{\circ}))):=\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}(D^{\circ}_{{\operatorname{Ran}}}))$ with an action of $\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}(D^{\circ}))$ .

#### 3.1.11.

The functor in Conjecture 1 is defined by

$$ \mathbf{Fact}({\mathbf{M}}):=\mathbf{Fact}(\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}(D^{\circ})))\otimes_{\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}(D^{\circ}))}{\mathbf{M}}. $$

### 3.2. Lisse sheaves

In this subsection we define and study lisse sheaves on $D^{\circ}$ . Even though in this paper we work in the de Rham context, in his subsection we give the definition in all three frameworks: Betti, de Rham, and etale. In the etale context we relax the condition $\operatorname{char}(k)=0.$

#### Definition 3.2.1.

- • In the Betti context, let $\Lisse(D^{\circ})^{\heartsuit}$ denote the abelian category of local systems of finite rank on $S^{1}$ , i.e. finite-dimensional vector spaces with an automorphism.

- • In the de Rham conext, let $\Lisse(D^{\circ})^{\heartsuit}$ denote the abelian category of finite rank free $k((t))$ -modules $V$ equipped with a $k$ -linear map

$$ \nabla:V\rightarrow Vdt $$

satisfying the Leibniz rule. Denote by $\Lisse(D^{\circ})$ the bounded derived category of $\Lisse(D^{\circ})^{\heartsuit}$ .

- • In the etale context, let $\Lisse(D^{\circ})^{\heartsuit}$ denote the abelian category of lisse $\ell$ -adic sheaves on $\Spec(k((t)))$ .

#### Lemma 3.2.2.

The category $\Lisse(D^{\circ})^{\heartsuit}$ has finite cohomological dimension.

#### Proof.

Let ${\mathcal{O}}$ be the unit. We need to check that the functor $\Hom_{\Lisse(D^{\circ})}({\mathcal{O}},-)$ has finite cohomological amplitude. But this functor commutes with colimits, hence it suffices show that for ${\mathcal{E}}\in\Lisse(D^{\circ})^{\heartsuit}$ the complex $\Hom_{\QLisse(D^{\circ})}({\mathcal{O}},{\mathcal{E}})$ is bounded.

- • In the Betti context, this object obviously lies in $\Vect^{\geq 0,\leq 1}$ .

- • In the de Rham context since we can compute cohomology via the de Rham complex this object lies in $\Vect^{\geq 0,\leq 1}$ .

- • In the etale context, since $\Spec k((t))$ is a $K(\pi,1)$ -scheme, we can can compute

$$ \Hom_{\QLisse(D^{\circ})}({\mathcal{O}},{\mathcal{E}}) $$

as cohomology of $\pi_{1}^{\operatorname{et}}(\Spec k((t)))$ with coefficients in the corresponding representation $V$ . Let us show that these cohomologies lie only in degrees 0 and 1. If ${\operatorname{char}}(k)=0$ the assertion is immediate. Assume that ${\operatorname{char}}(k)=p$ for some prime $p\neq\ell$ . The group $\pi_{1}^{\operatorname{et}}(\Spec k((t)))$ is an extension of $\prod_{q\neq p}{\mathbb{Z}}_{q}$ with a pro- $p$ group of wild inertia. In particular, we have an exact sequence

$$ P\rightarrow\pi_{1}^{\operatorname{et}}(\Spec k((t)))\rightarrow{\mathbb{Z}}_{\ell} $$

where $P$ is a profinite group whose finite quotients have orders coprime to $q$ . Then since $P$ does not have cohomologies with coefficients in ${\mathbb{Q}}_{\ell}$ -modules, we get that

$$ \Gamma(\pi_{1}^{\operatorname{et}}(\Spec e((t))),V)\cong\Gamma({\mathbb{Z}}_{\ell},V^{P}), $$

and the latter is computes by a two-term complex.

∎

#### Definition 3.2.3.

Define $\IndLisse(D^{\circ}):=\Ind(\Lisse(D^{\circ}))$ . The t-structure on $\Lisse(D^{\circ})$ uniquely extends to a t-structure on $\IndLisse(D^{\circ})$ compatible with filtered colimits.

#### Notation 3.2.4.

for an Abelian category $C^{\heartsuit}$ denote by $\Ind^{\heartsuit}(C^{\heartsuit})$ the Abelian category of functors between $C^{\heartsuit}$ and ${\operatorname{Sets}}$ that preserve fiber products.

#### Lemma 3.2.5.

The category $\IndLisse(D^{\circ})$ has the following properties:

- (1) $\IndLisse(D^{\circ})^{\heartsuit}\cong\Ind^{\heartsuit}(\Lisse(D^{\circ})^{\heartsuit})$ ,

- (2) the category $\IndLisse(D^{\circ})$ is left-complete,

- (3) the category $\IndLisse(D^{\circ})$ is the derived category of its heart, i.e.

$$ \IndLisse(D^{\circ})\xrightarrow{\sim}D(\Ind^{\heartsuit}(\Lisse(D^{\circ})^{\heartsuit})):=\QLisse(D^{\circ}). $$

#### Proof.

Part (1) is immediate. Property (2) follows from [AGK+22, Theorem E.1.3] and Lemma 3.2.2. We now prove (3). By (1) we have

$$ \IndLisse(D^{\circ})^{\geq-n}\rightarrow\QLisse(D^{\circ})^{\geq-n} $$

for every $n$ , and by (2) the source is left-complete. It suffices to check that the target is left-complete as well. We claim that for an Abelian category ${\mathcal{A}}$ of finite cohomological dimension the category $D(\Ind^{\heartsuit}({\mathcal{A}}))$ is left-complete. Property (3) now follows from Lemma 3.2.2. ∎

#### Remark 3.2.6.

The category $\QLisse(D^{\circ})$ mimics the category $\QLisse(X)$ of [AGK+22], which is defined as

$$ \QLisse(X)\cong D(\Ind^{\heartsuit}(\Lisse(X)^{\heartsuit})). $$

#### 3.2.7.

In Betti context we have $\QLisse(D^{\circ})$ is obviously a Tannakian category, with a fiber functor given by $\ev_{x}$ for $x\in S^{1}$ . Moreover, $\QLisse(D^{\circ})\cong\QLisse({\mathbb{G}}_{m})$ , so all the desired properties of this Tannakian category were checked in [AGK+22, 1.7.4]. We now study $\QLisse(D^{\circ})$ in de Rham and etale frameworks.

Recall that in de Rham context $\Lisse^{\heartsuit}({\mathbb{G}}_{m})$ can be identified with coherent modules over $k[t,t^{-1}]$ with connection. Hence by restricting modules we obtain a map

$$ \Lisse^{\heartsuit}({\mathbb{G}}_{m})\rightarrow\Lisse^{\heartsuit}(D^{\circ}). $$

In the etale context the inverse image functor defines

$$ \Lisse^{\heartsuit}({\mathbb{G}}_{m})\rightarrow\Lisse^{\heartsuit}(D^{\circ}). $$

Since in both contexts it the map is t-exact we get

$$ \QLisse({\mathbb{G}}_{m})\rightarrow\QLisse(D^{\circ}). $$

#### Proposition 3.2.8.

There exists a symmetric monoidal $t$ -exact section

$$ \QLisse(D^{\circ})\rightarrow\QLisse({\mathbb{G}}_{m}) $$

of the map (3.4).

#### Proof.

- • In the de Rham context, by [Kat87, Theorem 2.4.10] there exists a $t$ -exact symmetric monoidal section $\Lisse(D^{\circ})^{\heartsuit}\rightarrow\Lisse({\mathbb{G}}_{m})^{\heartsuit}$ . This induces the desired section by Remark 3.2.6.

- • In the etale context, the same agument works by [Kat86, Theorem 1.5.6].

∎

#### Remark 3.2.9.

For any point $x\in{\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ the composition

$$ \QLisse(D^{\circ})\rightarrow\QLisse({\mathbb{G}}_{m})\xrightarrow{\text{ev}_{x}}\Vect $$

defines a fiber functor, making $\QLisse(D^{\circ})$ a Tannakian category.

In order to apply the formalism of [AGK+22] in our local context we need to show that $\QLisse(D^{\circ})$ is a well-behaved Tannakian category. Namely, recall the notion of gentle Tannakian category from [AGK+22, 1.7.2]:

Let ${\mathbf{H}}$ be a symmetric monoidal category, equipped with a t-structure and a conservative t-exact symmetric monoidal functor $\oblv_{\mathbf{H}}$ to $\Vect$ . Note that the assumptions on $\oblv_{\mathbf{H}}$ imply that the t-structure on ${\mathbf{H}}$ is compatible with filtered colimits and right-complete. We will additionally assume that ${\mathbf{H}}$ is left-complete in its t-structure.

#### Definition 3.2.10.

Let ${\mathbf{H}}$ be as above. We will say that ${\mathbf{H}}$ is a gentle Tannakian category if the following conditions are satisfied:

- • The following classes of objects in ${\mathbf{H}}^{\heartsuit}$ coincide: (i) Objects contained in ${\mathbf{H}}^{c}\cap{\mathbf{H}}^{\heartsuit}$ ; (ii) Objects that are sent to compact objects in $\Vect$ by $\oblv_{\mathbf{H}}$ ; (iii) Dualizable objects.

- • The object ${\mathbf{1}}_{\mathbf{H}}$ has the following properties: (i) The functor $\Hom_{\mathbf{H}}({\mathbf{1}}_{\mathbf{H}},-)$ has a finite cohomological amplitude; (ii) For any ${\mathbf{h}}\in{\mathbf{H}}^{c}\cap{\mathbf{H}}^{\heartsuit}$ , the cohomologies of $\Hom_{\mathbf{H}}({\mathbf{1}}_{\mathbf{H}},{\mathbf{h}})\in\Vect$ are finite-dimensional.

- • The category ${\mathbf{H}}^{\heartsuit}$ is generated under colimits by ${\mathbf{H}}^{c}\cap{\mathbf{H}}^{\heartsuit}$ .

#### Lemma 3.2.11.

The Tannakian category $\QLisse(D^{\circ})$ is gentle.

#### Proof.

- • We first treat te de Rham situation. We begin by checking the first condition. Note that $\QLisse(D^{\circ})^{\heartsuit}\cong\Ind(\Lisse(D^{\circ})^{\heartsuit})$ . The class of objects $\QLisse(D^{\circ})^{c}\cap\QLisse(D^{\circ})^{\heartsuit}$ coincides with $\Lisse(D^{\circ})^{\heartsuit}$ . By construction the class of objects in $\QLisse(D^{\circ})^{\heartsuit}\cong\Ind(\Lisse(D^{\circ})^{\heartsuit})$ that are sent to finite-dimensional vector spaces under the fiber functor from Remark 3.2.9 coincides with $\Lisse(D^{\circ})^{\heartsuit}$ . Every object of $\Lisse(D^{\circ})^{\heartsuit}$ in $\QLisse(D^{\circ})^{\heartsuit}$ is dualizable, and since every dualizable object is compact the class of dualizable objects coincides with $\Lisse(D^{\circ})^{\heartsuit}$ . Hence we checked the first condition in the definition of a gentle Tannakian category. Let us check the second condition. Let ${\mathcal{O}}$ be the unit. We need to check that the functor $\Hom_{\QLisse(D^{\circ})}({\mathcal{O}},-)$ has finite cohomological amplitude. But this functor commutes with colimits, hence it suffices show that for ${\mathcal{E}}\in\Lisse(D^{\circ})^{\heartsuit}$ the complex $\Hom_{\QLisse(D^{\circ})}({\mathcal{O}},{\mathcal{E}})$ is bounded. The latter statement follows from Lemma 3.2.2. We also need to show that cohomologies of $\Hom_{\QLisse(D^{\circ})}({\mathcal{O}},{\mathcal{E}})$ are finite-dimensional. By Levelt-Turritin theorem ([BBDE, Theorem 2.1]) we can reduce to the case when ${\mathcal{E}}$ is one-dimensional. Let us first treat the case when ${\mathcal{E}}$ is non-trivial. Then $H^{0}$ vanishes tautologically, and $H^{1}$ is the dual space to the zeroth cohomology of the de Rham complex for ${\mathcal{E}}^{\vee}$ , hence also vanishes. The case of trivial ${\mathcal{E}}$ it is a direct computation to show that both $H^{0}$ and $H^{1}$ are one-dimensional. The third condition that $\QLisse(D^{\circ})^{\heartsuit}$ is generated under colimits by $\QLisse(D^{\circ})^{c}\cap\QLisse(D^{\circ})^{\heartsuit}$ is immediate from the fact that the former is $\Ind(\Lisse(D^{\circ})^{\heartsuit})$ and the latter is $\Lisse(D^{\circ})^{\heartsuit}$ . Lastly, recall that we proved in Lemma 3.2.5 that $\QLisse(D^{\circ})$ is left-complete.

- • In the etale situation, the same arguments work for all desired conditions apart from part (ii) of the second one. However, the fact that cohomologies of $\Hom_{\QLisse(D^{\circ})}({\mathcal{O}},{\mathcal{E}})$ are finite-dimensional follows from our description given in Lemma 3.2.2.

∎

### 3.3. Definition and geometry of $\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})$

In this subsection we define and study the stack $\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})$ . Again, in his subsection we work in all three frameworks: Betti, de Rham, and etale.

#### Definition 3.3.1.

We define the prestack of local systems with restricted variation on the punctured disk $\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})(S)$ by sending an affine scheme $S$ to the space of right t-exact symmetric monoidal functors

$$ \Rep(G)\rightarrow\QLisse(D^{\circ})\otimes\QCoh(S). $$

#### Remark 3.3.2.

Recall that for a gentle Tannakian category ${\mathbf{H}}$ in [AGK+22, 1.8.1] the stack $\mathbf{Maps}(\Rep(G),{\mathbf{H}})$ is defined such that for $S$ an affine scheme $S$ -points of $\mathbf{Maps}(\Rep(G),{\mathbf{H}})$ are right t-exact symmetric monoidal functors

$$ \Rep(G)\rightarrow{\mathbf{H}}\otimes\QCoh(S). $$

By 3.2.11 the stack $\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})$ is a particular case of the stack $\mathbf{Maps}(\Rep(G),{\mathbf{H}})$ defined in [AGK+22].

#### Lemma 3.3.3.

There exists a section of the restriction map $\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}({\mathbb{G}}_{m})\rightarrow\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})$ .

#### Proof.

Follows from Lemma 3.2.8. ∎

By Remark 3.3.2 the stack $\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})$ enjoys the properties of the stack $\mathbf{Maps}(\Rep(G),{\mathbf{H}})$ establised in [AGK+22]. We list them in the rest of this subsection.

#### Proposition 3.3.4.

The prestack $\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})$ is an etale stack, equal to a disjoint union of etale stacks each of which can be written as an etale-sheafified quotient by $G$ of an etale stack $Y$ with the following properties:

- a) $Y$ is locally almost of finite type;

- b) $Y^{red}$ is an affine, classical, reduced scheme;

- c) $Y$ is an ind-scheme.

- d) $Y$ is a formal affine scheme in the sence of [AGK+22, Remark 1.4.7].

#### Proof.

Follows from Lemma 3.2.11 and [AGK+22, Theorem 1.8.3]. ∎

#### Corollary 3.3.5.

$\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})$ is a prestack locally almost of finite type.

#### Proof.

By [Chapter 2 Corollary 2.5.7][GR17a], [GR17a, Chapter 2 Corollary 2.7.5(a)] and [GR17a, Chapter 2 Corollary 2.7.10] for every laft prestack ${\mathcal{X}}$ such that ${}^{\leq n}{{\mathcal{X}}}$ is truncated ${}^{\leq n}{{\mathcal{X}}^{\operatorname{et}}}$ is locally of finite type, where ${\mathcal{X}}^{\operatorname{et}}$ stands for etale sheafification.

Now since $Y$ is locally almost of finite type the prestack quotient of $Y$ by $G$ is locally almost of finite type. Moreover, since $Y$ is and ind-scheme by [GR17b, Chapter 2 Lemma 1.2.3] ${}^{\leq n}Y$ is truncated, and hence the prestack quotient of ${}^{\leq n}Y$ by ${}^{\leq n}G$ is truncated.

It is left to notice that by [AGK+22, 2.1.4] the stack $\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})$ is convergent. ∎

#### Corollary 3.3.6 ([AGK+22, Proposition 7.8.2, Corollary 7.8.8]).

The stack $\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})$ is 1-affine.

#### Lemma 3.3.7 ([AGK+22, Corollary 7.9.2, Theorem 7.9.6]).

The category $\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))$ is a compactly generated semi-rigid category.

### 3.4. $\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})$ vs $\LocSys_{G}(D^{\circ})$

The first goal of this subsection is to establish the following statement:

#### Theorem 3.5.

There exists a natural morphism $\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})\rightarrow\LocSys_{G}(D^{\circ})^{\operatorname{et}}$ , where $(-)^{\operatorname{et}}$ stands for sheafification in etale topology.

#### Remark 3.5.1.

Note that there are morphisms

$$ \LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})\rightarrow\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}({\mathbb{G}}_{m})\rightarrow\LocSys_{G}({\mathbb{G}}_{m}), $$

where the last prestack classifies all de Rham $G$ -local systems on the open curve ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ . The difficulty to be overcome is that $\LocSys_{G}({\mathbb{G}}_{m})$ does not map to $\LocSys_{G}(D^{\circ})^{\operatorname{et}}$ .

#### 3.5.2.

Let $\Bun_{G}({\mathbb{G}}_{m})^{+}\subset\Bun_{G}({\mathbb{G}}_{m})$ denote the substack whose $S$ -points are principal $G$ -bundles on $S\times{\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ which admit an extension to $S\times{\mathbb{A}}^{1}$ etale locally on $S$ . By [ABC+24, B.7.15] we do have a canonical morphism

$$ \LocSys_{G}({\mathbb{G}}_{m})^{+}\rightarrow\LocSys_{G}(D^{\circ})^{\operatorname{et}}, $$

where

$$ \LocSys_{G}({\mathbb{G}}_{m})^{+}=\Bun_{G}({\mathbb{G}}_{m})^{+}\times_{\Bun_{G}({\mathbb{G}}_{m})}\LocSys_{G}({\mathbb{G}}_{m}). $$

Then Theorem 3.5 is equivalent to the following statement:

#### Theorem 3.6.

The composite

$$ \LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})\rightarrow\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}({\mathbb{G}}_{m})\rightarrow\LocSys_{G}({\mathbb{G}}_{m})\rightarrow\Bun_{G}({\mathbb{G}}_{m}) $$

factors through $\Bun_{G}({\mathbb{G}}_{m})^{+}$ .

#### 3.6.1.

Let $H$ be the group associated to $\QLisse(D^{\circ})$ and its fiber functor by the Tannakian formalism. Two homomorphisms out of $H$ of particular interest to us.

- (1) The map

$$ H\rightarrow{\mathbb{G}}_{a} $$

corresponding to the full subcategory

$$ \Rep({\mathbb{G}}_{a})\cong\QLisse(D^{\circ})_{{\operatorname{triv}}}\hookrightarrow\QLisse(D^{\circ}) $$

generated by the unit ${\mathcal{O}}$ .

- (2) By Chevellay’s theorem, the full abelian subcategory

$$ \QLisse(D^{\circ})^{\heartsuit,ss}\hookrightarrow\QLisse(D^{\circ})^{\heartsuit} $$

of semi-simple objects is a tensor subcategory. Under the Tannakian formalism, it corresponds to the pro-reductive quotient

$$ H\rightarrow H^{{\operatorname{red}}}. $$

#### Lemma 3.6.2.

The map

$$ H\rightarrow{\mathbb{G}}_{a}\times H^{{\operatorname{red}}} $$

is an isomorphism.

#### Proof.

We need to show that the functor

$$ \Rep(H^{{\operatorname{red}}}\times{\mathbb{G}}_{a})^{\heartsuit}\rightarrow\Rep(H)^{\heartsuit} $$

is an equivalence of categories. It is essentially surjective by the Levelt–Turritin theorem ([BBDE, Theorem 2.1]). To see that it is fully faithful, note that as $H^{{\operatorname{red}}}$ is reductive, every indecomposible object of the LHS takes the form

$$ V\boxtimes J_{n}, $$

where $V$ is an indecomposible object of $\Rep(H^{{\operatorname{red}}})^{\heartsuit}$ and $J_{n}$ is a Jordan block. ∎

#### Proof of Theorem 3.6.

Let $\mathbf{Maps}(\Rep(G),\Rep(H^{{\operatorname{red}}}))$ denote the prestack obtained by replacing $\QLisse(D^{\circ})$ with $\Rep(H^{{\operatorname{red}}})$ in the definition of $\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})$ . By Lemma 3.6.2 we have a group homomorphism $H^{{\operatorname{red}}}\rightarrow H$ , which induces

$$ \LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})\rightarrow\mathbf{Maps}(\Rep(G),\Rep(H^{{\operatorname{red}}})). $$

We claim that the map (3.5) factors through $\mathbf{Maps}(\Rep(G),\Rep(H^{{\operatorname{red}}}))$ . For this it is sufficient to show that the symmetric monoidal functor

$$ \Rep(H^{{\operatorname{red}}})\otimes\Rep({\mathbb{G}}_{a})\cong\QLisse(D^{\circ})\rightarrow\QLisse({\mathbb{G}}_{m})\rightarrow D({\mathbb{G}}_{m})\rightarrow\QCoh({\mathbb{G}}_{m}) $$

factors through $\Rep(H^{{\operatorname{red}}})$ . This is clear because every ${\mathbb{G}}_{a}$ -torsor on ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ is trivial.

It remains to show that the morphism

$$ \mathbf{Maps}(\Rep(G),\Rep(H^{{\operatorname{red}}}))\rightarrow\Bun_{G}({\mathbb{G}}_{m}) $$

factors through $\Bun_{G}({\mathbb{G}}_{m})^{+}$ . The category $\Rep(H^{{\operatorname{red}}})$ is gentle Tannakian so we can apply results from [AGK+22] to $\mathbf{Maps}(\Rep(G),\Rep(H^{{\operatorname{red}}}))$ . Since $H^{{\operatorname{red}}}$ is reductive, by [AGK+22, Proposition 3.5.4], connected components of $\mathbf{Maps}(\Rep(G),\Rep(H^{{\operatorname{red}}}))$ have the form $\pt/\Stab_{G}(\varphi)$ for some $\varphi:Im(H)\rightarrow G$ . Thus we only need to check that the composites

$$ \pt\rightarrow\pt/\Stab_{G}(\varphi)\rightarrow\Bun_{G}({\mathbb{G}}_{m}) $$

factor through $\Bun_{G}({\mathbb{G}}_{m})^{+}$ . This holds because every $G$ -bundle on ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ is trivial for a connected $G$ . ∎

#### 3.6.3.

One of the structural result that is not known yet is the following

#### Conjecture 2.

The stack $\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})$ is a disjoint union of formal completions of a collection of pairwise non-intersecting closed substacks of $(\LocSys_{G}(D^{\circ})^{\operatorname{et}})^{{\operatorname{red}}}$ .

#### 3.6.4.

In the rest of this subsection we a result in the direction of Conjecture 2, which will be useful for us in the future.

#### Proposition 3.6.5.

The map

$$ \LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})\rightarrow\LocSys_{G}(D^{\circ})^{\operatorname{et}} $$

is a monomorphism (i.e., is a monomorphism of spaces when evaluated on any affine scheme).

#### Proof.

Note that by Example A.2.5 it suffices to show that

$$ \LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})\rightarrow(\hormerxJets(\BG))_{x} $$

is a monomorphism. We first check the condition on classical affine schemes. It is enough to show that $\QCoh(\Spec(A))\otimes\QLisse(D^{\circ})$ embeds fully faithfully into the category of $A((t))$ -modules with an $A$ -linear connection. To show this notice that $\QCoh(\Spec(A))\otimes\QLisse(D^{\circ})$ is compactly generated by objects of the form $A\boxtimes(c[i])$ with $c\in\Lisse(D^{\circ})^{\heartsuit}$ , $i\in{\mathbb{Z}}$ . So to show fully faithfulness it suffices to prove that the functor sends $A\boxtimes c$ with $c\in\Lisse(D^{\circ})^{\heartsuit}$ to compacts in $A((t))$ -modules with connection, and that the functor is fully faithful on the full subcategory spanned by these objects.

The first claim follows from the fact that the right adjoint to $A((t))\otimes_{k((t))}(-)$ commutes with infinite direct sums.

The second claim says that

$$ \Hom_{\QCoh(\Spec(A))\otimes\QLisse(D^{\circ})}(A\boxtimes c_{1},A\boxtimes c_{2})\cong\Hom_{A((t))\Mmod\text{with}\nabla}(A((t))\otimes_{k((t))}c_{1},A((t))\otimes_{k((t))}c_{2}) $$

with $c_{i}\in\Lisse(D^{\circ})^{\heartsuit}$ . This is equivalent to proving the equivalence

$$ \Hom_{\QLisse(D^{\circ})}(c_{1},A\otimes c_{2})\cong\Hom_{{A((t))\Mmod\text{with}\nabla}}(c_{1},A((t))\otimes_{k((t))}c_{2}). $$

By [BBDE, Theorem 2.1]we can reduce to the case when $c_{1}$ is irreducible, and then it is dualizable. Hence it suffices to prove

$$ \Hom_{k((t))\Mmod\text{with}\nabla}({\mathcal{O}},A\otimes c_{2})\cong\Hom_{k((t))\Mmod\text{with}\nabla}({\mathcal{O}},A((t))\otimes_{k((t))}c_{2}), $$

where ${\mathcal{O}}$ is $k((t))$ with trivial connection. Using [BBDE, Theorem 2.1] again we reduce to the case when $c_{2}$ is irreducible. In that case $c_{2}\cong\pi_{*}{\mathcal{L}}$ for $\pi$ a finite covering of the disc and ${\mathcal{L}}$ one-dimensional local system. Then by adjunction it suffices to prove the equivalence for $c_{2}$ one-dimensional, which is a direct computation.

Note that by construction the prestack $(\hormerxJets(\BG))_{x}$ is convergent, hence to prove the proposition it is enough to show that for a truncated affine scheme $\Spec(A)$ the natural map

$$ \LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})(\pi_{0}(A))\times_{(\hormerxJets(\BG))_{x}(\pi_{0}(A))}(\hormerxJets(\BG))_{x}(A)\leftarrow\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})(A) $$

is an isomorphism. If $A$ is 0-truncated the claim is immediate. If $A$ is 1-truncated note that for $f\in\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})(\pi_{0}(A))$ we have

$$ \{f\}\times_{(\hormerxJets(\BG))_{x}(\pi_{0}(A))}(\hormerxJets(\BG))_{x}(A)\cong\Gamma(D_{\pi_{0}(A),\nabla}\times_{{\mathbb{A}}^{1}_{\mathrm{dR}}}{\mathbb{G}}_{m,\mathrm{dR}},f^{*}\mathfrak{g}[1]\otimes_{\pi_{0}(A)}\pi_{1}(A)[1]). $$

On the other side of (3.6) we have

$$ \{f\}\times_{\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})(\pi_{0}(A))}\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})(A)\cong\Gamma_{dR}(\pi_{0}(A)((t)),f^{*}\mathfrak{g}[1]\otimes_{\pi_{0}(A)}\pi_{1}(A)[1]), $$

and the isomorphism (3.6) follows from Proposition A.1.8. For $n$ -truncated $A$ we conclude the claim by induction.

∎

### 3.7. Main result

#### Theorem 3.8.

There exists a fully faithful functor

$$ \mathbf{Fact}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}:\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))\mathbf{-ModCat}\rightarrow\Rep(G)\mathbf{-FactModCat} $$

that commutes with the forgetful functors from both sides to $\mathbf{DGCat}$ . Here

- - On the left-hand side $\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))$ is viewed as a monoidal category with usual tensor product. The left-hand side is the $(\infty,2)$ -category of modules for this monoidal category.

- - On the right-hand side $\Rep(G)$ is the DG category of representation of $G$ equipped with factorization algebra category structure coming from symmetric monoidal structure on $\Rep(G)$ .

#### 3.8.1.

As in Conjecture 1, the functor $\mathbf{Fact}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}$ is given by a certain factorization $\Rep(G)$ -module category, $\mathbf{Fact}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})))$ , equipped with a commuting action of $\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))$ . We define $\mathbf{Fact}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})))$ as the category of quasi-coherent sheaves on the prestack

$$ \LocSys_{G}(D^{\circ}_{{\operatorname{Ran}}})^{\operatorname{et}}\times_{\LocSys_{G}(D^{\circ})^{\operatorname{et}}}\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}). $$

### 3.9. Connection with Conjecture 1

The contents of this subsection are dependent on Conjecture 2.

#### 3.9.1.

Conjecture 2 implies that the pushforward along the map

$$ \LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})\rightarrow\LocSys_{G}(D^{\circ})^{\operatorname{et}} $$

admits arbitrary base change, therefore

#### Proposition 3.9.2.

For any prestack ${\mathcal{Y}}$ mapping to $\LocSys_{G}(D^{\circ})^{\operatorname{et}}$ one has

$$ \QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))\otimes_{\QCoh((\LocSys_{G}(D^{\circ})^{\operatorname{et}})}\QCoh({\mathcal{Y}})\cong\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})\times_{\LocSys_{G}(D^{\circ})^{\operatorname{et}}}{\mathcal{Y}}). $$

We are now ready to establish connection with Conjecture 1.

#### Lemma 3.9.3.

The restriction functor

$$ R:\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))\mathbf{-ModCat}\rightarrow\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}(D^{\circ}))\mathbf{-ModCat} $$

is fully faithful.

#### Proof.

For any ${\mathbf{C}}_{1},{\mathbf{C}}_{2}\in\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))\Mmod$ we need to show that

$$ \Maps_{\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))\mathbf{-ModCat}}({\mathbf{C}}_{1},{\mathbf{C}}_{2})\cong\Maps_{\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}(D^{\circ}))\mathbf{-ModCat}}(R({\mathbf{C}}_{1}),R({\mathbf{C}}_{2})). $$

We can write ${\mathbf{C}}_{1}\cong\text{colim}\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))\otimes{\mathbf{D}}_{i}$ for some plain DG categories ${\mathbf{D}}_{i}$ . Since $R$ is continuous we may assume that ${\mathbf{C}}_{1}\cong\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))\otimes{\mathbf{D}}$ for a plain DG category ${\mathbf{D}}$ . Then

$$ \Maps_{\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}(D^{\circ}))\mathbf{-ModCat}}(R({\mathbf{C}}_{1}),R({\mathbf{C}}_{2}))\cong $$

$$ \cong\Maps_{\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))\mathbf{-ModCat}}(\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))\otimes_{\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}(D^{\circ}))}\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))\otimes{\mathbf{D}},{\mathbf{C}}_{2}). $$

By Proposition 3.9.2 the latter is equivalent to

$$ \Maps_{\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))\mathbf{-ModCat}}(\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})\times_{\LocSys_{G}(D^{\circ})^{\operatorname{et}}}\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))\otimes{\mathbf{D}},{\mathbf{C}}_{2}). $$

Then Proposition 3.6.5 implies the desired claim. ∎

#### 3.9.4.

Combining Proposition 3.9.2 and Lemma 3.9.3, we get

#### Lemma 3.9.5.

The composite functor

$$ \mathbf{Fact}\circ R:\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))\mathbf{-ModCat}\rightarrow\Rep(G)\mathbf{-FactModCat} $$

coincides with $\mathbf{Fact}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}$ .

## 4. Reductions

### 4.1. Reduction to the case of ${\mathbb{A}}^{1}$

In this subsection we reduce Theorem 3.8 to the case when $X=\mathbb{A}^{1}$ , $x=0$ . We first record the following corollary of Theorem B.3:

#### Corollary 4.1.1.

Let $f:X\rightarrow Y$ be a map of curves with $x\in X,y\in Y$ such that $f(x)=y$ and $f$ is etale at $x$ . Then we have

$$ \Rep(G)-\mathbf{FactModCat}({\operatorname{Ran}}_{Y,y})\cong\Rep(G)-\mathbf{FactModCat}({\operatorname{Ran}}_{X,x}). $$

#### 4.1.2.

Note that every affine smooth curve $X$ admits a map $f:X\rightarrow{\mathbb{A}}^{1}$ etale at $x\in X$ . So we see that to reduce the problem to the case of ${\mathbb{A}}^{1}$ it suffices to check that the following diagram commutes:

$$ {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Rep(G)-\mathbf{FactModCat}({\operatorname{Ran}}_{{\mathbb{A}}^{1},0})} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{restr}(D^{\circ}))\mathbf{-ModCat}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Rep(G)-\mathbf{FactModCat}({\operatorname{Ran}}_{X,x}).} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong} $$

We conclude commutativity of (4.2) by the following statement:

#### Lemma 4.1.3.

Under the isomorphism (4.1) the object

$$ \QCoh({\LocSys_{G}}(D^{\circ}_{{\operatorname{Ran}}_{{\mathbb{A}}^{1}}})) $$

maps to

$$ \QCoh({\LocSys_{G}}(D^{\circ}_{{\operatorname{Ran}}_{X}})). $$

#### Proof.

Without loss of generality we may assume that $f$ is etale and surjective, and $f^{-1}(y)=\{x\}$ . Recall the definition of prestacks in question via Example A.2.5. Let $({X_{\mathrm{dR}}^{I}\times x})^{\circ}$ be the pullback

$$ {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces({X_{\mathrm{dR}}^{I}\times x})^{\circ}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X_{\mathrm{dR}}^{I}\times x} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\circ}}{{{{\operatorname{Ran}}}_{X_{\mathrm{dR}},x}}}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{Ran}}_{X_{\mathrm{dR}},x}.} $$

Our goal is to show that

$$ \hormerxJets(\BG^{{\operatorname{naive}}})_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}^{I}\times x}\times_{(X_{\mathrm{dR}}^{I}\times x)}({X_{\mathrm{dR}}^{I}\times x})^{\circ} $$

is isomorphic to

$$ \hormerxJets(\BG^{{\operatorname{naive}}})_{Y_{\mathrm{dR}}^{I}\times y}\times_{(Y_{\mathrm{dR}}^{I}\times y)}({X_{\mathrm{dR}}^{I}\times x})^{\circ}. $$

Let $x^{I}:S\rightarrow({X_{\mathrm{dR}}^{I}\times x})^{\circ}\subset X_{\mathrm{dR}}^{I}\times x$ and denote by $y^{I}$ composition $S\rightarrow Y_{\mathrm{dR}}^{I}\times y$ . We will show that

$$ D_{x^{I},\nabla}\times_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}(X-x)_{\mathrm{dR}}\cong D_{y^{I},\nabla}\times_{Y_{\mathrm{dR}}}(Y-y)_{\mathrm{dR}}. $$

To do that it suffices to show that there exists

$$ D_{x^{I},\nabla}\xrightarrow{\cong}D_{y^{I},\nabla} $$

that makes the diagram

$$ {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces D_{x^{I},\nabla}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X_{\mathrm{dR}}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces D_{y^{I},\nabla}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Y_{\mathrm{dR}}} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong} $$

commutative. From the Definition A.1.4 it follows that we need to show that $\Gamma_{f}:\Gamma_{x^{I,{\operatorname{red}}}}\xrightarrow{\cong}\Gamma_{y^{I,{\operatorname{red}}}}$ . We claim that this map is finite. Indeed, we have

$$ {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bigsqcup_{i\in(I+1)}S^{{\operatorname{red}}}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Gamma_{x^{I,{\operatorname{red}}}}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Gamma_{y^{I,{\operatorname{red}}}}} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\pi_{x}} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\pi_{y}} $$

with the obvious maps $\pi_{x}$ and $\pi_{y}$ . Now we note that all schemes are affine, ${\mathcal{O}}_{\Gamma_{y^{I,{\operatorname{red}}}}}$ is Noetherian, $\pi_{y}$ is finite, and ${\mathcal{O}}_{\Gamma_{x^{I,{\operatorname{red}}}}}\subset{\mathcal{O}}_{\bigsqcup_{i\in(I+1)}S^{{\operatorname{red}}}}$ , which gives that $\Gamma_{f}$ is finite. It is left to check that $\Gamma_{f}$ is bijection of $k$ -points, but this follows from the fact that $x$ mapped to $({X_{\mathrm{dR}}^{I}\times x})^{\circ}\subset X_{\mathrm{dR}}^{I}\times x$ . ∎

#### Corollary 4.1.4.

Under the isomorphism (4.1) the object

$$ \QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})\times_{\LocSys_{G}(D^{\circ})}{\LocSys_{G}}(D^{\circ}_{{\operatorname{Ran}}_{{\mathbb{A}}^{1}}})) $$

maps to

$$ \QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})\times_{\LocSys_{G}(D^{\circ})}{\LocSys_{G}}(D^{\circ}_{{\operatorname{Ran}}_{X}})). $$

#### Remark 4.1.5.

This argument reduced Conjecture 1 to the case of $X={\mathbb{A}}^{1},x=0$ .

For the duration of the main body of the paper we fix a notation $X={\mathbb{A}}^{1}$ , $x=0$ , $U={\mathbb{A}}^{1}\setminus x$ .

### 4.2. Reduction to the affine case I

Let ${\mathbf{C}}_{1}$ and ${\mathbf{C}}_{2}$ be DG categories acted on by $\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})$ . Theorem 3.8 asserts that the functor

$$ \operatorname{Fun}_{\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))}({\mathbf{C}}^{1},{\mathbf{C}}^{2})\rightarrow\operatorname{FactFun}_{\Rep(G)}(\mathbf{Fact}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}({\mathbf{C}}^{1}),\mathbf{Fact}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}({\mathbf{C}}^{2})) $$

is an equivalence.

#### 4.2.1.

In this subsection we will show that it suffices to prove (4.5) when ${\mathbf{C}}^{1}\cong\QCoh(R_{1})$ with $R_{1}$ an affine scheme, where the action of $\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})$ comes from a pullback along some map $R_{1}\rightarrow\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})$ . We begin with the following immediate property:

#### Lemma 4.2.2.

The functor $\mathbf{Fact}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}$ commutes with small colimits.

#### 4.2.3.

Thus we may assume that ${\mathbf{C}}^{1}\cong\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))\otimes{\mathbf{C}}_{0}^{1}$ , where ${\mathbf{C}}_{0}^{1}$ is a plain DG category. Suppose ${\mathbf{M}}^{1}:={\mathbf{N}}\otimes{\mathbf{M}}_{0}$ such that the action of $\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))$ comes from the first factor. Then we have

$$ \operatorname{Fun}_{\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))}({\mathbf{M}}^{1},{\mathbf{M}}^{2})\simeq\operatorname{Fun}({\mathbf{M}}_{0},\operatorname{Fun}_{\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))}({\mathbf{N}},{\mathbf{M}}^{2})) $$

and

$$ \operatorname{FactFun}_{\Rep(G)}(\mathbf{Fact}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}({\mathbf{M}}^{1}),\mathbf{Fact}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}({\mathbf{M}}^{2}))\simeq\operatorname{Fun}({\mathbf{M}}_{0},\operatorname{FactFun}_{\Rep(G)}(\mathbf{Fact}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}({\mathbf{N}}),\mathbf{Fact}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}({\mathbf{M}}^{2}))). $$

#### 4.2.4.

Thus we may assume that ${\mathbf{C}}_{0}^{1}$ is $\Vect$ . By Proposition 3.3.4 we have $\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})\cong((\sqcup Y_{i})/G)^{\operatorname{et}}$ , where $Y_{i}$ are formal affine schemes, so we can write

$$ \QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))\cong\QCoh(\sqcup Y_{i})^{G,w}, $$

where superscript $w$ stands for weak invariants in the sense of [Ber17].

#### Lemma 4.2.5.

Let ${\mathbf{A}}$ be a symmetric monoidal category, ${\mathbf{C}}\in{\mathbf{A}}\mathbf{-ModCat}$ . Assume also that ${\mathbf{C}}$ admits a weak action of a group $G$ of finite type. Then

$$ {\mathbf{C}}^{G,w}\cong{\mathbf{C}}_{G,w} $$

as ${\mathbf{A}}$ -modules.

#### Proof.

Follows directly from the case ${\mathbf{A}}=\Vect$ (see [Ber17, Corollary 2.3.5]). ∎

#### 4.2.6.

Hence by Lemma 4.2.5 we can reduce to the case ${\mathbf{C}}^{1}\cong\QCoh(\sqcup Y_{i})_{G,w}$ . Then we can write $\QCoh(\sqcup Y_{i})_{G,w}$ as a colimit of the bar resolution

$$ {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\ldots} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\QCoh(G)\otimes\QCoh(G)\otimes\QCoh(\sqcup Y_{i})} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\QCoh(G)\otimes\QCoh(\sqcup Y_{i})} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\QCoh(\sqcup Y_{i}),} $$

where the arrows are given by action, multiplication, and trivial action. Notice that since $\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))$ is semi-rigid all arrows in the diagram (4.6) are $\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))$ -linear. Therefore we may assume that

$$ {\mathbf{C}}^{1}\cong\QCoh(G^{n})\otimes\QCoh(\sqcup Y_{i}), $$

and thus that

$$ {\mathbf{C}}^{1}\cong\QCoh(G^{n}\times Y_{i}). $$

#### 4.2.7.

Now each $Y_{i}\times G^{n}$ is a formal affine scheme, so by [AGK+22, Corollary 7.3.4] we can write

$$ \QCoh(G^{n}\times Y_{i})\cong\text{colim}_{\AffSch_{/Y_{i}\times G^{n}}}\QCoh(S_{i}) $$

with affine $S_{i}$ , where the maps are given by pushforwards. Using semi-rigidity of $\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))$ we see that these maps are $\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})$ -linear, hence we obtain the desired reduction.

### 4.3. Reduction to the affine case II

In this subsection we will further reduce to the case when ${\mathbf{C}}^{2}\cong\QCoh(R_{2})\otimes{\mathbf{C}}_{0}^{2}$ . Here $R_{2}$ is an affine scheme, the action of $\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))$ comes from a map

and ${\mathbf{C}}_{0}^{2}$ is a plain DG category.

#### Proposition 4.3.1.

The functor $\mathbf{Fact}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}$ commutes with small limits.

#### Lemma 4.3.2.

Let $S$ be a prestack such that $\QCoh(S)$ is semi-rigid. Let

$$ \Phi:{\mathbf{A}}\rightleftarrows{\mathbf{A}}^{\prime}:\Psi $$

be an adjunction in $\mathbf{FactAlgCat}^{S}$ . Let ${\mathbf{C}}^{\prime}\in{\mathbf{A}}^{\prime}\mathbf{-FactMod}^{S}$ . #### Proof of Proposition 4.3.1.

Recall (see 3.8.1) that

$$ \mathbf{Fact}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}({\mathbf{M}}):={\mathbf{M}}\otimes_{\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))}\mathbf{Fact}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))). $$

$$ \mathbf{Fact}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})))_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}^{I}\times\{x\}} $$

is dualizable as a plain DG category for every $I$ .

We claim that by Proposition 4.4.4 we are in position to use Lemma 4.3.2. $$ \Rep(G)^{\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})} $$

on every strata follows from [Ras21a, Corollary 6.18.2]and [Che23, Lemma A.3.4]. ∎

#### 4.3.3.

By Barr-Beck-Lurie theorem we can write ${\mathbf{C}}^{2}$ as a colimit of the diagram

$$ {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\ldots} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))\otimes\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))\otimes{\mathbf{C}}^{2}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))\otimes{\mathbf{C}}^{2},} $$

where the maps are given by action and multiplication on $\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))$ . By definition of semi-rigidity and by [AGK+22, Lemma C.5.3] these maps admit continuous $\QCoh(\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ}))$ -linear right adjoints.

#### Lemma 4.3.4.

Let ${\mathbf{A}}$ be a semi-rigid symmetric monoidal category. Let $I$ be an $\infty$ -category, let $i\mapsto{\mathbf{C}}_{i}$ be a functor $I\rightarrow{\mathbf{A}}\mathbf{-ModCat}$ . For $\alpha:i\rightarrow j\in I$ denote the corresponding functor between ${\mathbf{C}}_{i}$ and ${\mathbf{C}}_{j}$ by $F_{\alpha}$ . Assume that for each $\alpha$ the functor

$$ \Oblv(F_{\alpha}):\Oblv({\mathbf{C}}_{i})\rightarrow\Oblv({\mathbf{C}}_{j}) $$

admits continuous right adjoint $\Oblv(G_{\alpha})$ , which is then upgrades to an ${\mathbf{A}}$ -linear functor $G_{\alpha}$ by semi-rigidity. Then

$$ \underset{I,F}{\text{colim}\text{ }}{\mathbf{C}}_{i}\cong\lim_{I^{\op},G}{\mathbf{C}}_{i} $$

Let us first check that the underlying DG categories are equivalent. Since

$$ \Oblv:{\mathbf{A}}\mathbf{-ModCat}\rightarrow\DGCat_{\text{cont}} $$

commutes with colimits we have

$$ \Oblv(\underset{I,F}{\text{colim}\text{ }}{\mathbf{C}}_{i})\cong\underset{I,\Oblv(F)}{\text{colim}\text{ }}\Oblv({\mathbf{C}}_{i}). $$

On the other hand since $\Oblv$ also commutes with limits we have that

$$ \Oblv(\lim_{I^{\op},G}{\mathbf{C}}_{i})\cong\lim_{I^{\op},\Oblv(G)}\Oblv({\mathbf{C}}_{i}). $$

But by [Gai, Lemma 1.3.3]we get

$$ \underset{I,\Oblv(F)}{\text{colim}\text{ }}\Oblv({\mathbf{C}}_{i})\cong\lim_{I^{\op},\Oblv(G)}\Oblv({\mathbf{C}}_{i}), $$

where the functor from left-hand side to right-hand side corresponds to the system of functors

$$ \prescript{\prime}{}{\ins_{j,\DGCat_{\text{cont}}}}:\Oblv({\mathbf{C}}_{j})\rightarrow\lim_{I^{\op},\Oblv(G)}\Oblv({\mathbf{C}}_{i}), $$

which are left adjoints to tautological functors

The latter functors are images under $\Oblv:{\mathbf{A}}\mathbf{-ModCat}\rightarrow\DGCat_{\text{cont}}$ of

$$ \ev_{j,{\mathbf{A}}\mathbf{-ModCat}}:\lim_{I^{\op},G}{\mathbf{C}}_{i}\rightarrow{\mathbf{C}}_{j}, $$

hence by semi-rigidity left adjoints $\prescript{\prime}{}{\ins_{i}}$ upgrade to ${\mathbf{A}}$ -linear functors left adjoint to $\ev_{j,{\mathbf{A}}\mathbf{-ModCat}}$ .

Therefore there exists an ${\mathbf{A}}$ -linear map

$$ \underset{I,F}{\text{colim}\text{ }}{\mathbf{C}}_{i}\rightarrow\lim_{I^{\op},G}{\mathbf{C}}_{i} $$

such that its image under $\Oblv$ is (4.7). But since (4.7) is an equivalence and $\Oblv$ is conservative we are done.

Therefore we have that for any affine $S$ a map $S\rightarrow\Omega^{1}(D^{\circ}_{{\operatorname{Ran}}})$ factors through $\Omega^{1,\leq n}(D^{\circ}_{{\operatorname{Ran}}})$ for some $n$ . Thus it suffices to check that

$$ \Omega^{1,\leq n}(D^{\circ}_{{\operatorname{Ran}}}))\rightarrow\operatorname{Ran}_{X_{\mathrm{dR}},x} $$

has an affine diagonal, which is immediate. ∎

#### Lemma 4.5.9.

Let $f:{\mathcal{X}}\rightarrow{\mathcal{Y}}$ be a morphism of prestacks which are sheaved in etale topology. Suppose that there exists a moprhism ${\mathcal{Y}}^{\prime}\rightarrow{\mathcal{Y}}$ which is affine and an etale covering. Then if the moprhism

$$ f^{\prime}:{\mathcal{X}}^{\prime}={\mathcal{X}}\times_{{\mathcal{Y}}}{\mathcal{Y}}^{\prime}\rightarrow{\mathcal{Y}}^{\prime} $$

has affine diagonal then so does $f$ .

#### Proof.

Note that

$$ {\mathcal{X}}^{\prime}\times_{{\mathcal{Y}}^{\prime}}{\mathcal{X}}^{\prime}\rightarrow{\mathcal{X}}\times_{{\mathcal{Y}}}{\mathcal{X}} $$

$$ {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{X}}^{\prime}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{X}}^{\prime}\times_{{\mathcal{Y}}^{\prime}}{\mathcal{X}}^{\prime}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{X}}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{X}}\times_{{\mathcal{Y}}}{\mathcal{X}}.} $$

We are in position to apply [GR17a, Chapter 2 Proposition 2.4.2], which gives the result. ∎

#### Lemma 4.5.10.

Let $f:{\mathcal{X}}\rightarrow{\mathcal{Y}}$ be a morphism of prestacks. Assume that for every affine $S$ mapping to ${\mathcal{Y}}$ the morphism $f_{S}:{\mathcal{X}}\times_{{\mathcal{Y}}}S\rightarrow S$ has an affine diagonal. Then $f$ has an affine diagonal.

#### Proof of Proposition 4.5.4.

Recall that $\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})$ is isomorphic to an etale sheafified quotient by $G$ of a certain etale stack ${\mathcal{Y}}$ . By Lemma 4.5.9 then it suffices to check that

$$ {\mathcal{Y}}\times_{\LocSys_{G}(D^{\circ})^{\operatorname{et}}}\LocSys_{G}(D^{\circ}_{{\operatorname{Ran}}})^{\operatorname{et}}\rightarrow{\mathcal{Y}}\times(\operatorname{Ran}_{X_{\mathrm{dR}},x})^{\operatorname{et}} $$

But recall that ${\mathcal{Y}}$ can be written as a filtered colimit $\text{colim}_{i}Y_{i}$ , where $Y_{i}$ are affine schemes. Therefore a map from an affine scheme $S$ to ${\mathcal{Y}}\times(\operatorname{Ran}_{X_{\mathrm{dR}},x})^{\operatorname{et}}$ factors through $Y_{i}\times(\operatorname{Ran}_{X_{\mathrm{dR}},x})^{\operatorname{et}}$ for some $i$ . $$ Y_{i}^{\prime}\times_{\LocSys_{G}(D^{\circ})^{\operatorname{et}}}\LocSys_{G}(D^{\circ}_{{\operatorname{Ran}}})^{\operatorname{et}}\cong Y_{i}^{\prime}\times_{(\Omega^{1}(D^{\circ})/G(D))^{\operatorname{et}}}(\Omega^{1}(D^{\circ}_{{\operatorname{Ran}}})/G(D)_{\operatorname{Ran}_{X_{\mathrm{dR}},x}})^{\operatorname{et}}, $$

and since $(\Omega^{1}(D^{\circ})/G(D))^{\operatorname{et}}$ has an afffine diagonal and $(\Omega^{1}(D^{\circ}_{{\operatorname{Ran}}})/G(D)_{\operatorname{Ran}_{X_{\mathrm{dR}},x}})^{\operatorname{et}}\rightarrow\operatorname{Ran}_{X_{\mathrm{dR}},x}$ has an affine diagonal (Lemma 4.5.8) the result follows. ∎

## 5. Proof of the main theorem

Consider the following diagram:

$$ {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\QCoh(T)} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\QCoh(T)} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\QCoh(R_{1}\times_{\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})}R_{2})} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{F_{\sigma_{2}}}^{*}{F_{\sigma_{1}}}_{*}(\omega_{U}\boxtimes{\mathcal{O}}_{T})\operatorname{-FactMod}^{T},} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sim} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Id} $$

where the left arrow is $*$ -pushforward along $p:R_{1}\times_{\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})}R_{2}\rightarrow T$ and the right arrow is taking the fiber at $x$ . Commutativity follows from the fact that $(-)_{\Rep(G)}$ and all reduction steps preserved forgetful functors.

Passing to left adjoints, we obtain a diagram that commutes up to a natural transformation

$$ {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\QCoh(T)} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\QCoh(T)} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\QCoh(R_{1}\times_{\LocSys_{G}^{{\operatorname{restr}}}(D^{\circ})}R_{2})} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{F_{\sigma_{2}}}^{*}{F_{\sigma_{1}}}_{*}(\omega_{U}\boxtimes{\mathcal{O}}_{T})\operatorname{-FactMod}^{T}.} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sim} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Id} $$

Let $M_{1}$ and $M_{2}$ denote the monads acting on $\QCoh(T)$ coming from left- and right-hand sides of the diagrams above. We have a map

### 5.1. Description of $M_{1}$

#### Lemma 5.1.1.

#### Remark 5.1.2.

## Appendix A Multidiscs and jets

### A.1. Discs

For an affine scheme $S$ fix a map $x^{I}:S\rightarrow X_{\mathrm{dR}}^{I}$ .

#### Definition A.1.1.

Define the formal disc $\widehat{D}_{x^{I}}$ as $(S\times X)^{\wedge}_{\Gamma_{f^{{\operatorname{red}}}}},$ where $\Gamma_{f^{{\operatorname{red}}}}$ is the pullback of the universal divisor along

$$ S^{{\operatorname{red}}}\rightarrow X^{I}\rightarrow\Div^{|I|}(X). $$

This prestack admits a canonical descent along $X\rightarrow X_{\mathrm{dR}}$ given by ${{\widehat{D}}_{x^{I},\nabla}}:=S^{\wedge}_{\Gamma_{f^{{\operatorname{red}}}}}$ .

#### Definition A.1.2.

Define the adic disc $D_{x^{I}}$ as the affinization of $\widehat{D}_{x^{I}}$ .

#### Remark A.1.3.

Note that affinization here is defined since $\widehat{D}_{x^{I}}$ is ind-affine.

This prestack also admits a canonical descent along $X\rightarrow X_{\mathrm{dR}}$ , denoted by $D_{x^{I},\nabla}$ . We will explain the name and give an explicit construction below. Let us note that the various formal discs can be assembled in the following diagram:

$$ {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\widehat{D}_{x^{I}}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces D_{x^{I}}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\widehat{D}}_{x^{I},\nabla}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces D_{x^{I},\nabla}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X_{\mathrm{dR}}.} $$

Now we need to define $D_{x^{I},\nabla}$ for ${x^{I}}:S\rightarrow X_{\mathrm{dR}}^{I}$ . Notice that naive definition

$$ D_{x^{I},\nabla}:=(D_{x^{I}})_{\mathrm{dR}} $$

will fail to produce the desired answer since even for $x:\pt\rightarrow X_{\mathrm{dR}}$ the diagram

$$ {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces D_{x}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces(D_{x})_{\mathrm{dR}}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X_{\mathrm{dR}}} $$

will not be Cartesian. Instead, we will produce the definition via writing down an action of the infinitesimal groupoid on $D_{x^{I}}$ .

#### Construction A.1.4.

For ${x^{I}}:S\rightarrow X_{\mathrm{dR}}^{I}$ define $D_{x^{I},\nabla}$ as follows. Consider the simplicial prestack

$$ \widehat{D}_{x^{I}}^{\bullet}:={\widehat{D}}_{x^{I},\nabla}\times_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}\hat{\Delta}_{\bullet}=S^{\wedge}_{\Gamma_{f^{{\operatorname{red}}}}}\times_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}\hat{\Delta}_{\bullet}, $$

where $\hat{\Delta}_{\bullet}$ is the Cech nerve of $X\rightarrow X_{\mathrm{dR}}$ . For each $n\in{\mathbb{N}}$ , restrict $\hat{D}_{x^{I}}^{\bullet}$ to the simplicial scheme $\Delta^{(n)}_{\bullet}$ , where $\Delta^{(n)}_{k}$ is the $n$ -th neighborhood of the main diagonal in $X^{k+1}$ , then take the affinization term-wise. Denote the result by ${D}_{x}^{(n),\bullet}$ .

Put $D_{x^{I},\nabla}=\text{colim}_{n}|{D}_{x^{I}}^{(n),\bullet}|.$

#### Remark A.1.5.

Since $S^{\wedge}_{\Gamma_{f^{{\operatorname{red}}}}}$ is naturally a prestack over $X_{\mathrm{dR}}$ we get that $D_{x^{I},\nabla}$ also lives over $X_{\mathrm{dR}}$ .

#### Lemma A.1.6.

For any ${x^{I}}:S\rightarrow X_{\mathrm{dR}}^{I}$ we have

$$ D_{x^{I},\nabla}\times_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}X\cong D_{x^{I}}. $$

#### Proof.

Consider the following framework. Let $S_{\bullet}$ be a simplicial prestack mapping to $\hat{\Delta}_{\bullet}$ . Call $S_{\bullet}$ Cartesian over $\hat{\Delta}_{\bullet}$ if

$$ S_{n}\times_{\hat{\Delta}_{n}}\hat{\Delta}_{n+1}\cong S_{n+1} $$

for any choice of projection $\hat{\Delta}_{n+1}\rightarrow\hat{\Delta}_{n}$ . We claim that in this case $|S_{\bullet}|\times_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}X\cong S_{0}$ as prestacks over $X$ . Indeed, if we view $X$ as a constant simplicial prestack over $X_{\mathrm{dR}}$ we get

$$ |S_{\bullet}|\times_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}X\cong|S_{\bullet}\times_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}X|. $$

We claim that

$$ S_{\bullet}\times_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}X\cong S_{0}\times_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}\hat{\Delta}_{\bullet} $$

as simplicial prestacks over $\hat{\Delta}_{\bullet}\times_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}X$ . Here $S_{\bullet}\times_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}X$ maps to $\hat{\Delta}_{\bullet}$ via projection to $S_{\bullet}$ and to $X$ via second projection, and $S_{0}\times_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}\hat{\Delta}_{\bullet}$ maps to $\hat{\Delta}_{\bullet}$ via second projection and to $X$ via projection to $S_{0}$ .

Let us introduce some notation. Let $p_{\hat{k}}$ be maps in the simplicial complex $\hat{\Delta}_{\bullet}$ , let $d_{\hat{k}}$ be maps in the simplicial complex $S_{\bullet}$ . Finally, let $\pi_{\bullet}$ denote the map $S_{\bullet}\rightarrow\hat{\Delta}_{\bullet}$ .

We proceed by constructing the isomorphism in three steps. First, Consider $S_{n}\times_{\hat{\Delta}_{n}}\hat{\Delta}_{n+1}$ , where $\hat{\Delta}_{n+1}$ maps to $\hat{\Delta}_{n}$ via $p_{\hat{1}}$ . This is a prestack over $\hat{\Delta}_{n}\times_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}X$ (it maps to $\hat{\Delta}_{n}$ via $\pi_{n}$ precomposed with projection and to $X$ via composition of projection to $\hat{\Delta}_{n+1}$ and projection of the latter to the first coordinate). Identity on $S_{n}$ and projection to the first coordinate on $\hat{\Delta}_{n+1}$ define an isomorphism

$$ S_{n}\times_{\hat{\Delta}_{n}}\hat{\Delta}_{n+1}\xrightarrow[\sim]{\text{}}S_{n}\times_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}X. $$

Now using that $S_{\bullet}$ is Cartesian over $\hat{\Delta}_{\bullet}$ we get an isomorphism over $\hat{\Delta}_{n}\times_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}X$

$$ (d_{\hat{1}},\pi_{n+1}):S_{n+1}\xrightarrow[\sim]{\text{}}S_{n}\times_{\hat{\Delta}_{n}}\hat{\Delta}_{n+1}. $$

Here $S_{n+1}$ si viewed as a prestack over $\hat{\Delta}_{n}\times_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}X$ via $(p_{\hat{1}}\circ\pi_{n+1},\pi_{0}\circ d_{1})$ , where $d_{1}:S_{n+1}\rightarrow S_{0}$ is the obvious map. Using again that $S_{\bullet}$ is Cartesian over $\hat{\Delta}_{\bullet}$ we get an isomorphism over $\hat{\Delta}_{n}\times_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}X$

$$ (d_{1},p_{\hat{1}}\circ\pi_{n+1}):S_{n+1}\xrightarrow[\sim]{\text{}}S_{0}\times_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}\hat{\Delta}_{n}. $$

Composition of the above three isomorphisms defines the desired (A.1), since it is compatible with the simplicial structure.

It is left to notice that $(\text{colim}_{n}{D}_{x^{I}}^{(n)})^{\bullet}$ is Cartesian over $\hat{\Delta}_{\bullet}$ by construction.

∎

#### Corollary A.1.7.

### A.2. Horizontal jets meromorphic at one point

#### A.2.7.

#### Lemma A.2.8.

$$ R^{R}({\mathcal{Y}})\cong\hormerxJets({\mathcal{Y}}). $$

#### Proof.

For $S$ affine with a map $x:S\rightarrow X_{\mathrm{dR}}$ we have

$$ \Maps_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}(S,R^{R}({\mathcal{Y}}))\cong\Maps_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}(|\text{colim}_{n}S\times_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}\Delta_{\bullet}^{(n)}|,R^{R}({\mathcal{Y}}))\cong $$

$$ \cong\lim_{k}\lim_{n}\Maps_{\Delta_{\bullet}^{(n)}}(S\times_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}\Delta_{\bullet}^{(n)},R^{R}({\mathcal{Y}})\times_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}\Delta_{\bullet}^{(n)}). $$

Since $\Delta_{\bullet}^{(n)}$ and $R^{R}({\mathcal{Y}})\times_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}\Delta_{\bullet}^{(n)}$ are affine this is the same as

$$ \lim_{k}\lim_{n}\Maps_{\Delta_{\bullet}^{(n)}}((S\times_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}\Delta_{\bullet}^{(n)})^{\aff},R^{R}({\mathcal{Y}})\times_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}\Delta_{\bullet}^{(n)})\cong\Maps_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}(D_{x,\nabla},R^{R}({\mathcal{Y}})). $$

Now using Lemma A.1.7 we get that this is the same as

$$ \Maps_{U_{\mathrm{dR}}}(D_{x,\nabla}\times_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}U_{\mathrm{dR}},{\mathcal{Y}}). $$

∎

#### Remark A.2.9.

The proof of Lemma A.2.8 implies that $D_{x,\nabla}$ can be thought of as the relative affinization of $S\rightarrow X_{\mathrm{dR}}$ . This is specific to the first power of $X_{\mathrm{dR}}$ .

### A.3. Horizontal jets meromorphic at one point: parametrized version

Let $B$ be a prestack affine over $X_{\mathrm{dR}}$ . Consider categories of prestacks affine over $B\times_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}U_{\mathrm{dR}}$ and $B$ and the functor

$$ R_{B}:{\mathcal{T}}\rightarrow{\mathcal{T}}\times_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}U_{\mathrm{dR}} $$

between them. Let ${\mathcal{Y}}$ be a prestack affine over $B\times_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}U_{\mathrm{dR}}$ .

#### Definition A.3.1.

For affine $S$ with a map $x:S\rightarrow B$ set $\hormerxJetsF_{\nabla,B}^{\mer,x_{0}}({\mathcal{Y}})(S)$ to be maps

$$ D_{x,\nabla}\times_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}U_{\mathrm{dR}}\rightarrow{\mathcal{Y}} $$

over $B$ .

#### Lemma A.3.2.

Assume that partially defined right adjoint $R_{B}^{R}$ to $R_{B}$ is defined on ${\mathcal{Y}}$ . Then for $x:S\rightarrow B$ with affine $S$ we have

$$ \Maps_{B}(S,R_{B}^{R}({\mathcal{Y}}))\cong\Maps_{B\times_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}U_{\mathrm{dR}}}(D_{x,\nabla}\times_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}U_{\mathrm{dR}},{\mathcal{Y}}). $$

In other words, $R_{B}^{R}({\mathcal{Y}})\cong\hormerxJetsF_{\nabla,B}^{\mer,x_{0}}({\mathcal{Y}})(S)$ .

#### Proof.

As in the proof of the Lemma A.2.8 we have

$$ \Maps_{B}(S,R_{B}^{R}({\mathcal{Y}}))\cong\Maps_{B}(D_{x,\nabla},R_{B}^{R}({\mathcal{Y}})). $$

Since $D_{x,\nabla}$ is affine over $X_{\mathrm{dR}}$ (Lemma A.1.7) and $B$ is affine over $X_{\mathrm{dR}}$ we see that $D_{x,\nabla}$ is affine over $B$ . Hence

$$ \Maps_{B}(D_{x,\nabla},R_{B}^{R}({\mathcal{Y}}))\cong\Maps_{B\times_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}U_{\mathrm{dR}}}(D_{x,\nabla}\times_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}}U_{\mathrm{dR}},{\mathcal{Y}}). $$

∎

By definition of factorization restriction as the 2-Cartesian lift (see [CF24, Theorem-Definition 6.0.2]) we get that the functor

$$ \tilde{q}^{\bullet}:\mathbf{A}-\mathbf{FactModCat}({\operatorname{Ran}}_{Y,y})\rightarrow\mathbf{B}-\mathbf{FactModCat}(\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\circ}}{{{{\operatorname{Ran}}}_{X,x}}}) $$

admits a right adjoint described as

$$ \Res_{\mu}\circ\tilde{q}_{*}, $$

where $\mu:\mathbf{A}\rightarrow q_{\bullet}\mathbf{B}\in\mathbf{FactAlg}({{\operatorname{Ran}}_{Y}})$ comes from the unit of adjunction.

So we need to check that

$$ \tilde{q}^{\bullet}\circ\Res_{\mu}\circ\tilde{q}_{\bullet}\xrightarrow{\cong}\Id $$

and

$$ \Id\xrightarrow{\cong}\Res_{\mu}\circ\tilde{q}_{\bullet}\circ\tilde{q}^{\bullet}. $$

We first claim that

$$ \tilde{q}^{\bullet}:\mathbf{A}-\mathbf{FactModCat}({\operatorname{Ran}}_{Y,y})\rightarrow\mathbf{B}-\mathbf{FactModCat}(\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\circ}}{{{{\operatorname{Ran}}}_{X,x}}}) $$

is conservative.

Indeed, factor $f:X\rightarrow Y$ as a composition of a surjective map $f_{1}:X\twoheadrightarrow Y_{1}$ and an open $j:Y_{1}\hookrightarrow Y$ . Then

$$ q:\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\circ}}{{{{\operatorname{Ran}}}_{X}}}\rightarrow{{\operatorname{Ran}}_{Y}} $$

factors as

$$ \stackrel{{\scriptstyle\circ}}{{{{\operatorname{Ran}}}_{X}}}{\mathrel{\to}^{q_{1}}}{\operatorname{Ran}}_{Y_{1}}\xhookrightarrow{j}{\operatorname{Ran}}_{Y}. $$

Then

$$ \widetilde{q_{1}}^{\bullet}:\mathbf{A}-\mathbf{FactModCat}({\operatorname{Ran}}_{Y_{1},y})\rightarrow\mathbf{B}-\mathbf{FactModCat}(\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\circ}}{{{{\operatorname{Ran}}}_{X,x}}}) $$

is conservative by surjectivity, and

$$ \tilde{j}^{\bullet}:\mathbf{A}-\mathbf{FactModCat}({\operatorname{Ran}}_{Y,y})\rightarrow\mathbf{A}-\mathbf{FactModCat}({\operatorname{Ran}}_{Y_{1},y}) $$

is an equivalence by descent.

Therefore it suffices to check only that (B.3) is an equivalence. Using (B.2) we can rewrite (B.3) as

$$ \Res_{q^{\bullet}(\mu)}\circ\tilde{q}^{\bullet}\circ\tilde{q}_{\bullet}\xrightarrow{\cong}\Id. $$

Note that the composition

$$ q^{\bullet}(\mathbf{A})\xrightarrow{q^{\bullet}(\mu)}q^{\bullet}q_{\bullet}(\mathbf{B})\xrightarrow{\epsilon}\mathbf{B}, $$

where the latter map comes from count of the adjunction, is the identity. Therefore to show that (B.5) is identity it suffices to show that

$$ \tilde{q}^{\bullet}\circ\tilde{q}_{\bullet}\cong\Res_{\epsilon}. $$

For this statement we may assume that $\mathbf{B}$ is any element of $\mathbf{FactAlgCat}(\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\circ}}{{{{\operatorname{Ran}}}_{X}}})$ . Indeed, since $q$ and $\widetilde{q}$ are etale for any

$$ \mathbf{N}\in\mathbf{B}-\mathbf{FactModCat}(\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\circ}}{{{{\operatorname{Ran}}}_{X,x}}}) $$

#### Remark B.3.1.

Everything in this subsection prior to Theorem B.3 works as is for factorization algebras and modules in $\D$ as opposed to $\mathbf{CrysCat}$ . The proof of Theorem B.3 in fact can be simplified in that case. Indeed, the morphisms (B.3) and (B.4) obviously become equivalences after taking cores, but the functor of taking cores is conservative.

## Appendix C Parameterized factorization patterns

### C.1. Parameterized crystals of categories

Let $S$ be a 1-affine prestack such that $\QCoh(S)$ is semi-rigid. The goal of this subsection is to set up a theory of crystals of categories parameterized by $S$ and derive properties of such needed for the proof of Theorem C.2.3.

#### Definition C.1.1.

Let $Y$ be a laft lax prestack. An $S$ -linear crystal of categories ${\mathbf{A}}$ on $Y$ consists of the following data:

- • For any $s:R\to Y$ with $R$ a finite type affine scheme, there is a $\D(R)\otimes\QCoh(S)$ -module DG category:

$$ {\mathbf{A}}_{s}\in\D(R)\otimes\QCoh(S)-\mathbf{ModCat}\cong\QCoh(S)-\mathbf{ModCat}(D(R)-\mathbf{ModCat}). $$

- • For any 2-cell $\textstyle{R\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$ $\scriptstyle{s}$ $\scriptstyle{\theta}$ $\textstyle{T\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$ $\scriptstyle{v}$ $\scriptstyle{t}$ $\textstyle{Y,}$ there is a functor

$$ \theta_{\dagger}:{\mathbf{A}}_{s}\to{\mathbf{A}}_{t} $$

intertwining the symmetric monoidal functor

$$ u^{!}\otimes\Id:\D(R)\otimes\QCoh(S)\to\D(T)\otimes\QCoh(S), $$

such that if $\theta$ is invertible, then the induced functor

$$ \D(T)\otimes_{\D(S)}{\mathbf{A}}_{s}\to{\mathbf{A}}_{t} $$

is an equivalence.

- • Certain higher compatibilities.

#### Example C.1.2.

We have the constant $S$ -linear crystal $\mathbf{Vect}_{Y}^{S}$ .

As usual, there are two notions of morphisms between crystals of categories on a lax prestack: lax ones and strict ones defined as in Definition 2.1.5. Denote by $\Maps(\mathbf{C},\mathbf{D})$ ( $\Maps_{{\operatorname{str}}}(\mathbf{C},\mathbf{D})$ ) the category of (strict) functors from ${\mathbf{C}}$ to ${\mathbf{D}}$ .

#### Notation C.1.3.

Let

$$ \mathbf{CrysCat}^{S}(Y),\;\mathbf{CrysCat}^{S}(Y)^{{\operatorname{str}}} $$

be the $(\infty,2)$ -category of crystals of categories on $Y$ , with 1-morphisms given by morphisms (resp. strict morphisms) between crystals of categories, and 2-morphisms given by natural transformations.

We now state the $S$ -linear avatars of claims in [CF24, Subsections A.2-A.4] and note that the proofs are completely similar.

#### Lemma C.1.4.

Colimits and finite limits in $\Maps_{{\operatorname{str}}}(\mathbf{C},\mathbf{D})$ and $\Maps(\mathbf{C},\mathbf{D})$ are calculated point-wise, i.e. for any affine $S$ with $s:S\rightarrow Y$ the functors

$$ \Maps_{{\operatorname{str}}}(\mathbf{C},\mathbf{D})\rightarrow\operatorname{Fun}_{\D(S)\otimes\QCoh(S)}(\mathbf{C}(s),\mathbf{D}(s)) $$

and

$$ \Maps(\mathbf{C},\mathbf{D})\rightarrow\operatorname{Fun}_{\D(S)\otimes\QCoh(S)}(\mathbf{C}(s),\mathbf{D}(s)) $$

commute with colimits and finite limits.

#### Corollary C.1.5.

The categories $\Maps(\mathbf{C},\mathbf{D})$ and $\Maps_{{\operatorname{str}}}(\mathbf{C},\mathbf{D})$ are presentable and stable.

#### Definition C.1.6.

Define (lax) global sections of $\mathbf{C}$ to be

$$ \Gamma_{{\operatorname{str}}}^{S}(Y,\mathbf{C}):=\Maps_{{\operatorname{str}}}(\mathbf{Vect}_{Y}^{S},\mathbf{C}), $$

$$ \Gamma^{S}(Y,\mathbf{C}):=\Maps(\mathbf{Vect}_{Y}^{S},\mathbf{C}), $$

#### Remark C.1.7.

For $Y\in\PreSt$ we have $\Gamma^{S}(Y,\mathbf{C})\cong\Gamma_{{\operatorname{str}}}^{S}(Y,\mathbf{C})$ .

#### Example C.1.8.

We have

$$ \D(Y)\otimes\QCoh(S)\cong\Maps(\mathbf{Vect}_{Y}^{S},\mathbf{Vect}_{Y}^{S})\cong\Gamma^{S}(Y,\mathbf{Vect}_{Y}^{S}). $$

#### Construction C.1.9.

For a morphism $f:\mathbf{Y_{1}}\rightarrow\mathbf{Y_{2}}$ in $\laxPreSt$ we have natural functors

$$ f^{\bullet}:\mathbf{CrysCat}^{S}(\mathbf{Y_{2}})\rightarrow\mathbf{CrysCat}^{S}(\mathbf{Y_{1}}), $$

and

$$ f^{\bullet}:\mathbf{CrysCat}^{S}(\mathbf{Y_{2}})^{{\operatorname{str}}}\rightarrow\mathbf{CrysCat}^{S}(\mathbf{Y_{1}})^{{\operatorname{str}}}. $$

We will call them the pullback functors.

#### Lemma C.1.10.

Let $p:Y\rightarrow Z$ be a schematic morphism of prestacks. Then the functor

$$ p^{\bullet}:\mathbf{CrysCat}^{S}(Z)^{{\operatorname{str}}}\rightarrow\mathbf{CrysCat}^{S}(Y)^{{\operatorname{str}}} $$

admits a right adjoint

$$ p_{\bullet}:\mathbf{CrysCat}^{S}(Y)^{{\operatorname{str}}}\rightarrow\mathbf{CrysCat}^{S}(Z)^{{\operatorname{str}}} $$

satisfying the base change property.

#### Proof.

Note that $\mathbf{CrysCat}$ is tensored over $\mathbf{DGCat}$ , and since

$$ p^{\bullet}:\mathbf{CrysCat}(Z)^{{\operatorname{str}}}\rightarrow\mathbf{CrysCat}(Y)^{{\operatorname{str}}} $$

is $\mathbf{DGCat}$ -linear it upgrades to a functor between $S$ -linear crystals of categories, which coincides with the pullback

$$ p^{\bullet}:\mathbf{CrysCat}^{S}(Z)^{{\operatorname{str}}}\rightarrow\mathbf{CrysCat}^{S}(Y)^{{\operatorname{str}}}. $$

Note that in general

$$ p_{\bullet}:\mathbf{CrysCat}(Y)^{{\operatorname{str}}}\rightarrow\mathbf{CrysCat}(Z)^{{\operatorname{str}}} $$

is lax $\mathbf{DGCat}$ -linear. However, for dualizable categories it is strict $\mathbf{DGCat}$ -linear, therefore using semi-rigidity of $\QCoh(S)$ the assertion follows from [CF24, Lemma A.1.6]. ∎

#### Construction C.1.11.

Since $\mathbf{Vect}_{Y}^{S}$ is the symmetric monoidal unit in $\mathbf{CrysCat}^{S}(Y)$ and by Lemma C.1.4 we get that

$$ \Gamma^{S}(Y,\mathbf{C}),\text{ }\Maps(\mathbf{C},\mathbf{D})\in\D(Y)\otimes\QCoh(S)-\mathbf{ModCat}. $$

#### Definition-Proposition C.1.12.

Let $p:Y\rightarrow Z$ be a finite type schematic morphism in $\laxPreSt$ such that for any $S\in\AffSch$ the map $Y(S)\rightarrow Z(S)$ is a Cartesian fibration fibered in $\infty$ -groupoids. Then:

- (1) The functor

$$ p^{\bullet}:\mathbf{CrysCat}^{S}(Z)\rightarrow\mathbf{CrysCat}^{S}(Y) $$

admits a right adjoint

$$ p_{\bullet}:\mathbf{CrysCat}^{S}(Y)\rightarrow\mathbf{CrysCat}^{S}(Z) $$

satisfying the base change property;

- (2) The adjoint pair $(p^{\bullet},p_{\bullet})$ in $(1)$ extends one in Lemma C.1.10. More precisly, both functors in $(1)$ preserve strict morphisms, and for any

$$ \mathbf{C}\in\mathbf{CrysCat}^{S}(Y),\text{ }\mathbf{B}\in\mathbf{CrysCat}^{S}(Z) $$

the counit and unit

$$ p^{\bullet}\circ p_{\bullet}(\mathbf{C})\xrightarrow{\rho(\mathbf{C})}\mathbf{C},\text{ }\mathbf{B}\xrightarrow{\mu(\mathbf{B})}p_{\bullet}\circ p^{\bullet}(\mathbf{B}) $$

are contained respectively in $\mathbf{CrysCat}^{S}(Y)$ and $\mathbf{CrysCat}^{S}(Z)$ ;

- (3) If $p$ is etale (see [CF24, Definition A.3.1]), then $\mathbf{B}\xrightarrow{\mu(\mathbf{B})}p_{\bullet}\circ p^{\bullet}(\mathbf{B})$ has a right adjoint

$$ p^{\bullet}\circ p_{\bullet}(\mathbf{B})\xrightarrow{\varrho(\mathbf{B})}\mathbf{B} $$

contained in $\mathbf{CrysCat}^{S}(Z)$ , which is functorial in $\mathbf{B}$ .

#### Proof.

Follows from [CF24, Proposition-Definition A.3.3] by the same argument as in Lemma C.1.10. ∎

### C.2. Parameterized factorization patterns

#### Notation C.2.1.

We can define, parallel to notions described in Section 2, the following evident categories:

- (1) Set $\mathbf{FactAlgCat}^{S}$ , and call its objects $S$ -linear factorization categories over ${\operatorname{Ran}}^{ch}$ ,

- (2) For ${\mathbf{A}}\in\mathbf{FactAlgCat}^{S}$ set $\operatorname{FactAlg}^{S}({\mathbf{A}})$ , and call its objects $S$ -linear factorization algebras over ${\operatorname{Ran}}^{ch}$ ,

- (3) Set $\mathbf{FactModCat}^{S},$

- (4) For $\mathbf{A}\in\mathbf{FactAlgCat}^{S}$ set

$$ \mathbf{A}-\mathbf{FactModCat}^{S}, $$

- (5) For $({\mathbf{A}},{\mathbf{M}})\in\mathbf{FactModCat}^{S}$ and $A\in\operatorname{FactAlg}^{S}({\mathbf{A}})$ set

$$ A\operatorname{-FactMod}^{S}({\mathbf{M}}). $$

#### Remark C.2.2.

To get rigorous definitions of the above objects, note that $\mathbf{CrysCat}^{S}$ is an example of a $\mathbf{Type}$ (as in [CF24, Subsection 1.2]), so the formalism [CF24, Section 1-3] applies.

Having established results about $\mathbf{CrysCat}^{S}$ is subsection C.1 we get that the main theorem of [CF24] upgrades to the following statement.

#### Theorem-Definition C.2.3 ([CF24]).

The forgetful functor

$$ \mathbf{FactModCat}^{S}\to\mathbf{FactAlgCat}^{S} $$

is a (1,2)-Cartesian fibration. Given a morphism $\Phi:{\mathbf{A}}_{1}\to{\mathbf{A}}_{2}$ in the target, we denote the contravariant transport functor along $\Phi$ by

$$ \mathbf{Res}^{S}_{\Phi}:{\mathbf{A}}_{2}\mathbf{-FactModCat}^{S}\to{\mathbf{A}}_{1}\mathbf{-FactModCat}^{S}, $$

and call it the $S$ -linear factorization restriction functor along $\Phi$ . Moreover, for ${\mathbf{C}}_{2}\in{\mathbf{A}}_{2}\mathbf{-FactModCat}^{S}$ , there is a canonical equivalence

$$ \mathbf{Res}^{S}_{\Phi}({\mathbf{C}}_{2})_{x}\simeq\Phi(\operatorname{unit}_{{\mathbf{A}}_{1}})\operatorname{-FactMod}^{S}({\mathbf{C}}_{2}). $$

In particular, if $\Phi$ is strictly unital, then $\mathbf{Res}^{S}_{\Phi}({\mathbf{C}}_{2})$ and ${\mathbf{C}}_{2}$ have equivalent cores.

#### Remark C.2.4.

Exactly as in [CF24, Lemma 6.3.2 and 4.4] we have that $\mathbf{Res}^{S}_{\Phi}$ can be computed as a limit.

As in [CFGY24] we get

#### Corollary C.2.5.

Let $\Phi:{\mathbf{A}}\to{\mathbf{A}}^{\prime}$ be a morphism in $\mathbf{FactAlgCat}^{S}$ and ${\mathbf{C}}^{\prime}\in{\mathbf{A}}^{\prime}\mathbf{-FactModCat}^{S}$ . Let ${\mathcal{A}}\in\operatorname{FactAlg}^{S}({\mathbf{A}})$ . Then there is a canonical equivalence

$$ {\mathcal{A}}\operatorname{-FactMod}(\mathbf{Res}^{S}_{\Phi}({\mathbf{C}}^{\prime}))\simeq\Phi({\mathcal{A}})\operatorname{-FactMod}({\mathbf{C}}^{\prime}). $$

#### Definition C.2.6.

Let ${\mathbf{A}}$ be an $S$ -linear factorization algebra category and ${\mathbf{C}}$ be an $S$ -linear factorization ${\mathbf{A}}$ -module category. Let $\phi:{\mathcal{A}}_{1}\to{\mathcal{A}}_{2}$ be a morphism in $\operatorname{FactAlg}^{S}({\mathbf{A}})$ , viewed as a 2-morphism in $\mathbf{FactAlgCat}$ . Then the contravariant transport for (C.1) along this 2-morphism defines a factorization $(\Vect\otimes\QCoh(S))_{{\operatorname{Ran}}}$ -linear functor

$$ \mathbf{Res}^{S}_{{\mathcal{A}}_{2}}((\Vect\otimes\QCoh(S))_{{\operatorname{Ran}}})\to\mathbf{Res}^{S}_{{\mathcal{A}}_{1}}((\Vect\otimes\QCoh(S))_{{\operatorname{Ran}}}). $$

The core of it is a functor

$$ {\mathcal{A}}_{2}\operatorname{-FactMod}^{S}({\mathbf{C}})\to{\mathcal{A}}_{1}\operatorname{-FactMod}^{S}({\mathbf{C}}) $$

which we denote by $\operatorname{Res}^{S}_{\phi}$ and call it the factorization restriction functor along $\phi$ .

As in [CFGY24, Lemma B.8.1] we get

#### Lemma C.2.7.

Let

$$ \Phi:{\mathbf{A}}\rightleftarrows{\mathbf{A}}^{\prime}:\Psi $$

be an adjunction in the 2-category $\mathbf{FactAlgCat}^{S}$ . Then $\Phi$ is strictly unital.

The following result follows from Theorem-Definition C.2.3 and straightening, and is a direct generalization of [CFGY24, Theorem B.8.2]. We call it the basic $S$ -linear adjunction for factorization restrictions.

#### Theorem C.3.

Let $\Phi:{\mathbf{A}}\rightleftarrows{\mathbf{A}}^{\prime}:\Psi$ be an adjunction in the 2-category $\mathbf{FactAlgCat}^{S}$ . Then there is a canonical adjunction in $\mathbf{BiCat}_{\infty}$ :

$$ \mathbf{Res}^{S}_{\Phi}:{\mathbf{A}}^{\prime}\mathbf{-FactModCat}^{S}\rightleftarrows{\mathbf{A}}\mathbf{-FactModCat}^{S}:\mathbf{Res}^{S}_{\Psi}. $$

#### Remark C.3.1.

Let $\Phi:{\mathbf{A}}\rightleftarrows{\mathbf{A}}^{\prime}:\Psi$ be an adjunction in the 2-category $\mathbf{FactAlgCat}^{S}$ . Note that

- (1) For ${\mathbf{C}}^{\prime}\in{\mathbf{A}}^{\prime}\mathbf{-FactModCat}^{S}$ , the core of $\mathbf{Res}^{S}_{\Phi}({\mathbf{C}}^{\prime})$ is equivalent to that of ${\mathbf{C}}^{\prime}$ because $\Phi$ is strictly unital.

- (2) For ${\mathbf{C}}\in{\mathbf{A}}\mathbf{-FactModCat}^{S}$ , the core of $\mathbf{Res}^{S}_{\Psi}({\mathbf{C}})$ is equivalent to $\Psi(\operatorname{unit}_{{\mathbf{A}}})\operatorname{-FactMod}^{S}({\mathbf{C}})$ .

Hence we can formulate the basic adjunction as the following equivalence:

$$ \operatorname{FactFun}_{{\mathbf{A}}}({\mathbf{C}}^{\prime}_{x},{\mathbf{C}}_{x})\simeq\operatorname{FactFun}_{{\mathbf{A}}^{\prime}}({\mathbf{C}}^{\prime}_{x},\Psi(\operatorname{unit}_{{\mathbf{A}}})\operatorname{-FactMod}^{S}_{{\mathbf{C}}_{x}}), $$

where we use the point of view of factorization module categories concentrated at $x$ (rather than supported on ${\operatorname{Ran}}$ ).

#### Corollary C.3.2.

Let

$$ (\Phi,\Xi):({\mathbf{A}},{\mathbf{C}})\rightleftarrows({\mathbf{A}}^{\prime},{\mathbf{C}}^{\prime}):(\Psi,\Upsilon) $$

be an adjunction in $\mathbf{FactModCat}^{S}$ such that $\Xi$ and $\Upsilon$ induce equivalences between the cores of ${\mathbf{C}}$ and ${\mathbf{C}}^{\prime}$ . Then the factorization ${\mathbf{A}}$ -linear functor

$$ \Xi^{\operatorname{enh}}:{\mathbf{C}}\to\mathbf{Res}^{S}_{\Phi}({\mathbf{C}}^{\prime}) $$

induced by $\Xi$ is an equivalence.

#### Proof.

Generalizes directly from [CFGY24, Corollary B.8.4] and results in Subsection C.1. ∎

A converse to Corollary C.3.2 is also true, namely

#### Corollary C.3.3.

Let

$$ \Phi:{\mathbf{A}}\rightleftarrows{\mathbf{A}}^{\prime}:\Psi $$

be an adjunction in $\mathbf{FactAlgCat}^{S}$ . Let ${\mathbf{C}}^{\prime}\in{\mathbf{A}}^{\prime}\mathbf{-FactModCat}^{S}$ . Then there the natural map

$$ (\Phi,\Xi):({\mathbf{A}},\mathbf{Res}^{S}_{\Phi}({\mathbf{C}}^{\prime}))\rightarrow({\mathbf{A}}^{\prime},{\mathbf{C}}^{\prime}) $$

admits a right adjoint, denoted by $(\Psi,\Upsilon)$ .

We deduce the claim from Theorem-Definition C.2.3 and the following construction.

#### Construction C.3.4.

Let $\pi:{\mathbf{E}}\to{\mathbf{B}}$ be a $(1,2)$ -Cartesian fibration and $f:x\rightleftarrows y:g$ be the adjunction in ${\mathbf{B}}$ . Let $v$ be an element over $y$ . We will construct a right adjoint in ${\mathbf{E}}$ to the map

$$ L:f^{\dagger}(v)\rightarrow v. $$

Consider the 2-morphism $e:fg\rightarrow\Id_{y}$ and the 1-morphism $\Id_{v}$ over $\Id_{y}$ . Pulling back $\Id_{v}$ along $e$ we obtain $e^{\dagger}(\Id_{v}):v\rightarrow v$ over $fg$ . This morphism factors through $f^{\dagger}(v)$ , so we obtain a morphism $R:v\rightarrow f^{\dagger}(v)$ . We claim that $R$ is right adjoint to $L$ .

Indeed, the morphism $e^{\dagger}(\Id_{v})\rightarrow\Id_{v}$ gives $LR\rightarrow\Id_{v}$ , this is the counit of the desired adjunction. Now consider the 2-morphism $f\rightarrow fgf\rightarrow f$ . Note that the composition is $\Id_{f}$ . Pulling back $L$ , we obtain $L\rightarrow e^{\dagger}(\Id_{v})\circ L\rightarrow L$ . But since $L$ is a Cartesian arrow, the first morphism

$$ L\rightarrow e^{\dagger}(\Id_{v})\circ L\cong LRL $$

must be the horizontal composition of a 2-morphism $\Id_{f^{\dagger}(v)}\rightarrow RL$ with $\Id_{L}$ . This 2-morphism

$$ \Id_{f^{\dagger}(v)}\rightarrow RL $$

is the desired unit of the adjunction. The axioms of adjunction follow by unwinding the definitions.

#### Corollary C.3.5.

The functor

$$ \mathbf{Res}^{S}_{\Phi}:{\mathbf{A}}^{\prime}\mathbf{-FactModCat}^{S}\rightarrow{\mathbf{A}}\mathbf{-FactModCat}^{S} $$

is $\mathbf{DGCat}$ -linear.

#### Proof.

Let ${\mathbf{D}}\in\mathbf{DGCat}$ . Then by Corollary C.3.3 we get an adjunction

$$ (\Phi,\Xi\otimes\Id_{{\mathbf{D}}}):({\mathbf{A}},\mathbf{Res}^{S}_{\Phi}({\mathbf{C}}^{\prime})\otimes{\mathbf{D}})\rightleftarrows({\mathbf{A}}^{\prime},{\mathbf{C}}^{\prime}\otimes{\mathbf{D}}):(\Psi,\Upsilon\otimes\Id_{{\mathbf{D}}}). $$

But now Corollary C.3.2 implies that $\mathbf{Res}^{S}_{\Phi}({\mathbf{C}}^{\prime})\otimes{\mathbf{D}}\cong\mathbf{Res}^{S}_{\Upsilon\otimes\Id_{{\mathbf{D}}}}({\mathbf{C}}^{\prime}\otimes{\mathbf{D}})$ , as desired. ∎

#### C.3.6.

Let $\mathbf{A}$ be an $S$ -linear factorization category, and $\mathbf{C}$ be an $S$ -linear factorization $A$ -module category. Let $\mathbf{C}_{x}$ denote the fiber of $\mathbf{C}$ . Denote by $i_{{\operatorname{Ran}}_{X,x}}^{!}\otimes\Id_{\QCoh(S)}$ the restriction functor $\mathbf{C}\rightarrow\mathbf{C}_{x}$ . Let $U=X\setminus x$ . Let $j_{{\operatorname{Ran}}}^{!}\otimes\Id_{\QCoh(S)}$ denote the restriction functor

$$ \mathbf{C}\rightarrow\mathbf{C}|_{\Ranu\times x}. $$

Let $A\in\mathbf{A}$ be an $S$ -linear factorization algebra.

#### Proposition C.3.7.

Let $c\in\mathbf{C}_{x\times S}$ be such that the partially defined left adjoint ${j_{{\operatorname{Ran}}}}_{!}\otimes\Id_{\QCoh(S)}$ is defined on

$$ A\boxtimes_{S}c\in\mathbf{C}|_{\Ranu\times x}. $$

Then the partially defined left adjoint $\ind_{A}^{S}$ to forgetful functor

$$ A\operatorname{-FactMod}^{S}(\mathbf{C})\rightarrow\mathbf{C}_{x_{0}\times S} $$

is defined on $c$ . We have

$$ \ind_{A}^{S}(c)\cong({j_{{\operatorname{Ran}}}}_{!}\otimes\Id_{\QCoh(S)})(A\boxtimes_{S}c). $$

#### Proof.

Analogous to [CFGY24, Lemma 5.3.3]. ∎
